definition: One of the strategy-making variables measured; the authors write that 'Strategy making was described by: proactiveness, risk taking, product-market innovation, analysis, multiplexity, integration, futurity, consciousness of strategies, adaptiveness, and industry expertise.'

name: Consciousness of strategies
definition: One of the strategy-making variables measured; the authors write that 'Strategy making was described by: proactiveness, risk taking, product-market innovation, analysis, multiplexity, integration, futurity, consciousness of strategies, adaptiveness, and industry expertise.'

name: Adaptiveness
definition: One of the strategy-making variables measured; the authors write that 'Strategy making was described by: proactiveness, risk taking, product-market innovation, analysis, multiplexity, integration, futurity, consciousness of strategies, adaptiveness, and industry expertise.'

name: Industry expertise
definition: One of the strategy-making variables measured; the authors write that 'Strategy making was described by: proactiveness, risk taking, product-market innovation, analysis, multiplexity, integration, futurity, consciousness of strategies, adaptiveness, and industry expertise.'

name: Organizational size
definition: Kimberly (1976b) identifies four different aspects of size: physical capacity (the amount of production or work the organization is capable of doing as determined by its physical plant), personnel available (the finite amount of labor with which the organization has to do its work), the volume of inputs and outputs, and discretionary resources such as those indicated by net assets or wealth. The problem with administrative personnel is that they are involved in activities that relate to all aspects of size identified by Kimberly.

name: Administrative component
definition: Consistent with the preceding discussion and the personnel available measure of size, administrators are categorized as instructional or noninstructional.

name: Personnel components
authors_terms: ["personnel components", "other personnel components", "professional personnel", "teachers", "instructional secretaries/clerks", "noninstructional secretaries/clerks", "noninstructional personnel"]
definition: This study also is concerned with comparing what happens to various personnel components other than administrators in growing and declining organizations.

name: Growth and decline
definition: A declining school district is defined as one that realized a decrease in enrollment every year since 1968, and a growing district is one that realized an increase in each year. School districts showing a combination of increases and decreases were classified as mixed.

name: Executive tenure
authors_terms: ["executive tenure", "tenure of the chief executive", "tenure of the chief executive officer", "terms of office"]
definition: Executive tenure, taken from McEachern, was the years spent as chief executive as of December 1972.

name: Ownership type
definition: Firms were classified by McEachern into three ownership classes: owner managed, those for which stock ownership was concentrated among its managers; management controlled, for which stock ownership was dispersed among many shareholders; and externally controlled, for which stock ownership was concentrated among a few individuals who did not manage the firm.

name: Firm performance
authors_terms: ["operating performance", "performance in the capital market", "profit margin", "total return on common stock", "combined rate of return on common stock"]
definition: Two measures of firm performance were analyzed, operating performance and performance in the capital market. Profit margin, net income as a percentage of sales, is an indicator of the operating performance of firms; capital market performance was estimated as the combined rate of return on common stock, considering all dividends as being reinvested.

name: Proportion of inside directors
authors_terms: ["proportion of inside directors on the board", "proportion of insiders on the board", "board composition"]
definition: The proportion of inside directors on the board, the proportion of directors who were managers in 1972, is usually thought to reflect management domination of the board.

name: Scanlon Plan success
authors_terms: ["SP success", "rated SP success", "rated Scanlon Plan success"]
definition: For the purposes of this study, SP success is the extent to which the full effort, experience, creativity, and innovative ability of the entire work force through the use of the SP is directed toward increasing the organization's total effectiveness.

name: Scanlon Plan retention
authors_terms: ["whether the SP was subsequently abandoned or retained", "subsequent retention/abandonment of the SP", "subsequently succeeds", "subsequently fails"]
definition: Scanlon Plan success was also measured by whether the SP was subsequently abandoned or retained.

name: Participation in decision making
definition: Employee participation is the increased employee influence in the immediate job situation, plus a two tier committee system for processing those suggestions that involve more than just the individual's job. A high level of employee participation in decision making is treated as essential to SP success.

name: Company size
definition: Company size is the total number of employees.

name: Scanlon Plan tenure
authors_terms: ["number of years a company has had the Scanlon Plan", "time", "number of years a company has maintained an SP"]
definition: The number of years a company has had the Scanlon Plan.

name: Managerial attitudes toward participative management policies
authors_terms: ["managerial attitudes", "average managerial attitude toward participative management policies", "MA"]
definition: Attitudes of all persons with supervisory responsibilities toward participative management policies, assessed with Miles's instrument for attitudes relating to his human resources management style.

name: CEO attitudes toward participative management policies
definition: The attitude of the most senior executive(s) toward participative management policies.

name: Rewards for participative management
authors_terms: ["reward for following participative management policies", "perceived rewards for following participative policies"]
definition: The extent to which managers thought they would be recognized and not criticized for following participative management policies.

name: Expected Scanlon Plan success
authors_terms: ["expected level of SP success", "expectations of success before the plan is implemented"]
definition: The extent to which employees thought the SP would contribute to achieving various desirable outcomes, measured before the plan is begun.

name: Agency budget size
definition: The amount of money allocated to an agency for the 1972-73 fiscal year by the state or federal government. The authors treat a large financial resource base (budget) as conducive to establishing a highly diversified organization set.

name: Breadth of services
authors_terms: ["breadth of services", "broad range of services", "wide scope of services"]
definition: The range of services an agency provides to its clients; when an organization is providing a wide range of supportive services to its clients, in addition to basic services such as training, employment placement, and counseling, the organization interacts with a larger and more diverse set of organizations.

name: Instrumental value of organization set
authors_terms: ["INSTVALUE", "instrumental value", "perceived instrumental value", "goodness of fit between the perceived utility of an agency's linkages and the number of linkages it has established"]
definition: The degree to which an agency's established linkages correspond to the perceived instrumental value of the interacting organizations. The authors examine cases in which the number of linkages an agency has established with a group of organizations is not consistent with the administrator's perceived instrumental value of that type of organization.

name: Organization set size
authors_terms: ["organization set size", "size of the organization set", "number of linkages"]
definition: The total number of local organizations, public and nonprofit, with which a focal manpower organization interacts.

name: Organization set diversity
definition: The spread of an agency's linkage partners across the sectors of its task environment. The authors describe a large and diversified (the opposite of concentrated) organization set, and measure concentration with Herfindahl's 'H' statistic.

name: Voluntary association memberships
authors_terms: ["voluntary association memberships", "membership in local voluntary organizations", "staff's membership in voluntary organizations", "civic action organizations"]
definition: The average number of civic action organizations (e.g., NAACP, Settlement House Board) the staff members belong to. Membership is argued to increase social integration in the community and provide information regarding the interests and resources held by others.

name: Previous jobs in other organizations
authors_terms: ["previous jobs in other organizations", "staff's previous jobs", "previously held several positions in other organizations"]
definition: The average number of previous jobs the staff held in employment service, other manpower organizations, business organizations, public agencies, education organizations, and other community service type organizations. The authors argue that visibility and legitimacy may result from staff members' previously holding positions in other local organizations.

name: Staff meetings
definition: The number of regularly scheduled meetings within an organization per month. The authors suggest staff meetings are used in the agencies studied as an important mechanism for exchanging information about the task environment.

name: Centralization of authority
definition: The concentration of authority to make linkage-relevant decisions rather than delegating it to boundary spanners. The authors expect centralization of authority to result in an organization set with an overall higher quality of relationships because key decisions are based on a broad scope of information about the various resource controlling alternatives.

name: Perceived control over the environment
authors_terms: ["perceived control over the environment", "perception of their ability to control the environment", "organization dominates its environment"]
definition: The staff's perception of the organization's control over its environment, measured by asking the agency's director to respond to a survey question with a 7-point response scale ranging from 'the environment dominates the organization' to 'the organization dominates its environment.'

name: Perceived importance of interacting organizations
authors_terms: ["perceived importance", "perceived importance of the task environment", "perceived importance of interacting organizations"]
definition: A rating of the perceived importance of each of the nine sectors for the successful fulfillment of the agency's mission, obtained from the agency's director. Each sector was rated on a 7-point scale.

name: Designed structure
definition: Structure obtained from organization charts, personnel records, and other available documents or through interviews with key informants, e.g., a top manager; Sathe concluded that institutional measures tap designed structure.

name: Emergent structure
definition: Structure indicated by the responses of a sample of organization members to a questionnaire, aggregated in some fashion; Sathe concluded that questionnaire measures tap emergent structure.

name: Formalization
definition: One of the three structural dimensions measured in the study; institutionally it is measured by Inkson, Pugh and Hickson's documentation index and by questionnaire with a rules and procedures scale.

name: Centralization
definition: One of the three structural dimensions measured in the study; institutionally it is measured by Samuel and Mannheim's hierarchy of control index and the average number of hierarchical levels, and by questionnaire with a centralization scale and a participation in decision making scale.

name: Differentiation
definition: One of the three structural dimensions measured in the study; institutionally it is measured by the number of discrete functions, the number of job titles, and Samuel and Mannheim's functional diversification index, and by questionnaire with a division of labor scale.

name: Organizational context
definition: Third factors, such as context, that could confound the relationship between institutional and questionnaire measures of structure; the context factors considered here are subunit size, technology, and environment.

name: Submit size
definition: Department size, measured as the logarithm of the total number of full time personnel in the department.

name: Technology routineness
definition: Department technology, measured with a routineness scale administered to department members.

name: Environmental uncertainty
definition: Perceived environmental uncertainty, measured using Sathe's (1974) scale administered to department heads, a modification of Duncan's (1971) scale.

name: Environmental configuration
definition: The three environmental dimensions investigated in this research were complexity, change rate, and routineness of problem/opportunity states. These dimensions were used to arrive at the eight-cell typology.

name: Environmental complexity
definition: As used in this study, environmental complexity refers to the number and heterogeneity/diversity of factors and components that the focal unit has to contend with in decision making.

name: Change rate
definition: Change rate refers to the frequency and magnitude of turbulence that prevails among environmental factors and components.

name: Routineness of problem/opportunity states
authors_terms: ["routineness of problem/opportunity states", "nonroutineness of problem/opportunity states"]
definition: The routineness of problem/opportunity states dimension refers to the variability and analyzability of the stimuli confronting the organizational unit.

name: Perceived environmental uncertainty
definition: The three components making up or contributing to the decision maker's perception of environmental uncertainty are: (1) lack of information regarding environmental factors, (2) not knowing the outcome of a specific decision, and (3) not being able to assign probabilities.

name: Departmental structure
definition: Departmental structure was defined and measured in terms of the degree of standardization (Hage & Aiken, 1967), formalization, role specialization (Pugh et al., 1969), and the degree of decentralization in decision making (Taylor & Bower, 1972).

name: Time perspective taken in planning
authors_terms: ["time perspective taken in planning", "time perspective", "planning perspective"]
definition: The time perspective adopted by his department in planning future policies and goals to be pursued by the department.

name: Frequency of changes to plans
authors_terms: ["frequency of changes to plans", "frequency of changes/modifications to existing policies and programs"]
definition: The frequency of changes to existing departmental plans and programs over the lifetime of such policies and programs.

name: Extraorganizational communication
authors_terms: ["extra-organizational communication", "extra-unit communication", "external technical communication", "mean level of extraorganizational communication", "mean frequency of technical communication outside of the organization", "communication with colleagues outside the organization"]
definition: The study focused on the amount of communication between project members and professionals outside the organization (i.e., researchers in universities, those met at professional society conferences, and technical consultants).

name: Communication skew across project members
authors_terms: ["degree to which extra-organizational communication is skewed across project members", "skew in external communication", "degree of skew", "degree to which outside technical communication is skewed across project members"]
definition: To the extent that project members rely on gatekeepers for technical information, there should be substantial positive intraproject skew in external communications. If, however, gatekeepers do not exist, then the skew in external communication will not be substantial; there will be a more even distribution of extra-organizational communication.

name: Project performance
definition: A group of top level managers helped develop a set of specific dimensions that would tap the more general categories of project goal achievement, integration, and adaptability. Performance dimensions included: schedule, budget and cost performance, innovativeness, adaptability, and the ability to cooperate with other areas in the large organization.

name: Project task type
authors_terms: ["project task type", "task dimension ranging from more universal (research) to more locally defined (technical service)", "nature of the subunit's work", "project's work"]
definition: In R&D settings, tasks can differ by (1) length of time required for feedback; (2) specific problem versus general problem orientation; and (3) their generation of new knowledge in contrast to their use of existing knowledge. With these attributes, the following task categories were developed with the laboratory's management to form a task dimension ranging from more universal (research) to more locally defined (technical service).

name: Organization size
definition: Size of the school district is measured as the number of students; number of students represents the demands placed upon such organizations by the community.

name: Organizational affluence
definition: Revenues per pupil are the measure of district affluence; they control for the size of the district and indicate whether the relative size of the total resource pie is larger or smaller than other districts.

name: Employee education
authors_terms: ["employee education", "teacher education", "educational level of employees", "educational level of employees in the technical core"]
definition: Educational level of employees in the technical core is measured as the percentage of teachers in the district who have a master's degree. To some extent, employee education represents power relationships in the organization.

name: Resource allocation to the technical core
authors_terms: ["technical core", "proportion of resources allocated to the technical core", "proportion of resources allocated to teaching"]
definition: Core departments represent the primary purpose of the organization and typically provide services or products for consumption by the organization's clients; in high schools the primary function is classroom teaching, so resources devoted to that activity are considered allocated to the technical core.

name: Resource allocation to overhead functions
authors_terms: ["overhead functions", "proportion of resources allocated to overhead", "administration, clerical and maintenance", "total overhead"]
definition: Overhead functions are those that support the organization itself and whose services are consumed within the organization; the proportion of resources allocated to administration, clerical and maintenance indicates the relative cost of all overhead activities in the district.

name: Resource allocation to auxiliary educational services
definition: Proportion of total salaries paid to provide services to students in support of classroom education; these services closely support classroom teaching and are auxiliary to the technical core.

name: Resource allocation to other student and community services
definition: Proportion of total salaries paid to personnel involved in other student and community programs, which include adult education, summer school, lunch, athletics, manpower development and training, and economic opportunity project.

name: Division self-containment
definition: A high self-containment organization is one in which divisions contain all key personnel and facilities necessary to deal with their particular product-market environments. Low self-containment organizations are those in which significant aspects of key functions—e.g., R&D, sales, purchasing, manufacturing, long-range planning—are provided by central units or shared among sister divisions.

name: Divisionalization
definition: Divisionalization refers to the pattern formed by the size, number, and product-market scopes of a company's divisions. A highly divisionalized organization is characterized by a large number of relatively small divisions with single industry or narrower scopes of responsibility.

name: Complexity of coordinative devices
definition: The range and relative importance of systems, roles, and groups superimposed on the basic organization structure to maintain communication and control between the headquarters and divisions and among divisions.

name: Divisionalized organization type
definition: A type is a distinct combination of the underlying organizational choices (division self-containment, divisionalization, and complexity of coordinative devices); the taxonomy contained 18 possible types of divisionalized organization, 15 of which were required to classify the situations in the data base.

name: General management influence over divisional policies
authors_terms: ["influence over divisional policies", "general management influence networks", "influence networks", "influence of various management groups"]
definition: The influence over divisional policies exerted by five levels or groups of executives who typically have general management responsibilities; the dependent behavioral variable in hypothesis 2.

name: Corporate technological staff size
authors_terms: ["corporate-level technological staff size", "corporate technological staff size", "corporate-level technological staffs"]
definition: Any group engaged in basic research, engineering, product development, or process improvement in such a way that less than 50 percent of its activities resulted in direct external sales, its activities were designed to benefit at least half of the firm's operating divisions, and no more than 50 percent of its activities were undertaken for the exclusive benefit of any one operating division.

name: Leader initiating structure
definition: The extent to which the leader is perceived as defining and structuring his role and those of his subordinates toward goal attainment.

name: Leader consideration
definition: The extent to which the leader is seen as having job relationships characterized by mutual trust, respect for subordinates' ideas, and consideration of their feelings.

name: Organizational size
authors_terms: ["organizational size", "agency size", "number of full-time organization members"]
definition: The definition of organizational size used here, which is consistent with earlier formulations, is the number of full-time organization members. Size is used as a measure of organizational formalization or bureaucratization.

name: Job satisfaction
authors_terms: ["job satisfaction", "employee job satisfaction", "satisfaction with the supervisor"]
definition: Measured by the Job Descriptive Index, which contains measures of five dimensions of job satisfaction (work, supervision, co-workers, pay, and promotion).

name: Work motivation
definition: Motivation operationalized from the expectancy model, which specifies two linkages between individual effort and the attainment of work outcomes and requires the measurement of expectancy, instrumentality and valence.

name: Job-induced tension and anxiety
authors_terms: ["job-induced tension and anxiety", "job-related tension and anxiety", "job related tension and anxiety"]
definition: A 13-item scale factorially derived by Rizzo, House and Lirtzman (1970).

name: Propensity to leave
definition: A single-item measure asking how often in the past six months the respondent has seriously considered the possibility of getting a job elsewhere.

name: Turnover rate
authors_terms: ["actual turnover rates", "turnover rates", "total turnover rate", "resignation rate", "transfer rate"]
definition: Objective rates of full-time employees who left the agency during the past 12 months relative to the total number of authorized full-time agency employees.

name: Leader performance appraisal
authors_terms: ["appraised job performance of the agency director", "performance appraisal of the agency director", "performance evaluation"]
definition: The agency director's most recent performance evaluation, including graphic ratings on quality of work, quantity of work, cooperation, initiative, maintenance of equipment and supplies, and the manner in which the county director directed, reviewed and checked the work of the unit.

name: Organizational size
definition: The measure of organizational size is the number of members in the local administrative bureaucracy.

name: Structural complexity
authors_terms: ["organizational structural complexity", "structural complexity", "shape of the organization", "width", "vertical differentiation", "height"]
definition: Two measures of structural complexity were used to tap the shape of the organization, width and vertical differentiation. Structural complexity is indicative of high differentiation, which may either reduce the need for constant communication or require coordination that entails a high level of communication.

name: Routineness of technology
authors_terms: ["routinization", "routineness of technology", "degree of routinization of work processes", "technology"]
definition: The measure of technology used here reflects the orientation of Hage and Aiken (1969) and Perrow (1967), which locates technology at the level of individual tasks; a primary dimension of technology is the routinization of the work activity.

name: Decentralization of authority
definition: Decentralization of authority was measured by examining the reported authority of organizational actors in making 18 strategic decisions. Strategic decisions refer to those decisions which were concerned with policy matters.

name: Boundary spanning
authors_terms: ["organizational boundary spanning activity", "boundary spanning", "organizational permeability", "boundary spanning roles", "openness"]
definition: The authors define boundary spanning roles as those roles which link the focal organizations in a social system and which are directly relevant for the goal attainment of the focal organization; organizational permeability has traditionally been defined as boundary spanning activity.

name: Department head communication
authors_terms: ["frequency of department head communication", "department head communication"]
definition: The frequency of verbal communication of department heads, with the paper concentrating on the frequency of downward, upward and lateral communication.

name: Subordinate communication
definition: The frequency of verbal communication of subordinates, with the paper concentrating on the frequency of downward, upward and lateral communication.

name: Organizational size
authors_terms: ["size", "population of the area serviced by the bus system", "number of buses owned by the system"]
definition: The independent variable size was measured in two ways: the population of the area serviced by the bus system and the number of buses owned by the system. Hall (1972) contends that measures of size are largely interchangeable.

name: Centralization of authority
definition: Centralization of authority is one of the three aspects of structure examined in the study. The measure of centralization of authority was obtained by multiplying the number of final decisions made at each level by a weight assigned to that level and summing for all levels.

name: Operations autonomy
definition: Operations autonomy was defined as the proportion of final decisions made by the resident operations manager and his staff, which includes any decisions delegated by him to his subordinates.

name: Number of administrative levels
definition: The number of levels was determined by counting the hierarchical positions on the organization chart provided by each property in the sample.

name: Structural type
definition: Three organizational types distinguished by the arrangement of upper and middle management: in type I, upper and middle management are existing government entities; in type II, upper management is an existing government entity and middle management is a specially created authority or board for transit matters; in type III, a special transit board or authority assumes both top and middle management responsibility.

name: Perceived prestige
definition: Organization sets develop a prestige order which provides their more prestigious members with certain advantages. A perceived prestige ranking was obtained from the Carpenter et al. (1974) survey of accounting educators, who assessed the quality of accounting faculties in departments offering doctoral degrees.

name: Coalition formation
definition: Coalition is defined as the combination of two or more organizations to achieve their operational goals and is the most constraining form of interorganizational cooperation. In this research, coalition formation among accounting departments is measured by the degree of hiring by each department of the accounting doctoral graduates of other departments.

name: Vertical integration
definition: Instead of forming coalitions to acquire the scarce resource externally within the organization set, the organization will produce its own resource internally; with respect to faculty personnel, the process of vertical integration would be referred to as inbreeding, the hiring of one's own graduates as faculty.

name: Geographic location
definition: To the extent physical opportunity for interorganizational cooperation exists within the organization's external environment, such cooperation becomes more likely, a theoretical base in the concept of propinquity; by virtue of being geographically located within the same region, the paths of certain members of the university organization set will continually cross.

name: Openness to interhospital cooperation
authors_terms: ["openness to cooperation", "openness to programs of interhospital cooperation", "hospital administrator openness"]
definition: The degree of willingness of the administrator to consider activities involving interhospital cooperation as a legitimate and important hospital operating goal.

name: Perceived hospital performance
authors_terms: ["perceived level of hospital task accomplishment", "administrator perceptions of hospital performance distress", "perceptions of hospital levels of task accomplishment", "perceived hospital performance levels"]
definition: The administrator's evaluation of hospital task performance on cost, efficiency, quality and growth dimensions. The hypothesis is framed in terms of performance distress, which is the low end of this dimension.

name: Professional activity
authors_terms: ["level of professional identification", "index of state and local professional activity", "professional identification", "state and local professional activity"]
definition: An administrator's degree of participation in health-related professional activities, operationalized as participation at the national level and participation at the state and local levels.

name: Boundary-spanning behavior
definition: Involvement in actual interchanges across organizational boundaries, as well as a more cognitive factor indicating a general awareness of organizational interdependencies. The authors state the third hypothesis was developed with this dual notion of boundary-spanning behavior in mind.

name: Supportive organizational climate
authors_terms: ["supportiveness of the organizational climate", "supportive climate", "organizational climate"]
definition: Organizational climate refers to a set of measurable properties of the work environment, perceived directly or indirectly by the people who live and work in this environment and assumed to influence their motivation and behavior. A supportive climate is characterized by high levels of trust and confidence between superiors and subordinates, multidirectional rather than just vertical communication, cooperative teamwork among workgroup members, a reasonable degree of subordinate involvement in decision-making and general goal setting, and an emphasis on self-control rather than superior-imposed control.

name: Managerial assessment of MBO effectiveness
authors_terms: ["managers' assessment of the effectiveness of MBO", "MBO effectiveness", "assessment of MBO effectiveness"]
definition: MBO is defined as a process whereby each manager establishes and works toward achieving specific objectives in key areas of his job responsibility during a specified time period. Managers' assessments of MBO effectiveness were measured in terms of several benefits of MBO suggested by the conceptual and/or empirical literature.

name: Type of work
authors_terms: ["type of work", "nature of a manager's job", "line and staff"]
definition: Type of work was divided into the traditional categories of line and staff, with differentiation made on the basis of whether the job essentially contributed directly to the products or service of the company (line) or indirectly in more of an advisory capacity (staff).

name: Organization level
definition: Organization level was divided into middle and lower management, where the former group included department, district, and manager levels and the latter group consisted of first-line supervisors.

name: Need for independence
definition: An individual's need for independence can be viewed as his desire to think and behave in a relatively autonomous manner, reflected in the person's wish to make his own decisions, to implement these decisions, and to exercise a good deal of self-control over his activities.

name: Interorganizational community
definition: A grouping of competing organizations linked by informal interpersonal interfirm communications such that it can be studied as a social group. The authors set four criteria: informal communication channels linking the firms together in the graph theoretic sense, interconnections dense enough to resemble known social groupings, interconnections shown to be other than random, and frequency-of-use data indicating that the networks are used on some regular basis.

name: Informal interorganizational communication network
definition: Informal, interpersonal, interfirm communications in a competitive industry designed to elicit information to be used in a major innovation adoption decision, expressed as regular opinion/advice relationships and information-seeking contacts among decision makers.

name: Firm similarity
authors_terms: ["similarity in the firms' size and type of business", "firm size", "type of business"]
definition: Resemblance among firms in size and in type of business. The authors argue that the patterning of interaction follows similarity, as in human society where social interaction is often based on similarities in interests, background and aspirations.

name: Opinion leadership
definition: The extent to which other firms turn to a firm for information and advice concerning the innovation.

name: Centrality in opinion/advice networks
definition: A firm's position in the informal opinion/advice network, indexed by the number of opinion/advice nominations it received from other firms in the industry.

name: Time of adoption
authors_terms: ["time of adoption", "early adopters", "later adopters", "date that a decision was made to adopt"]
definition: The date on which a firm decided to adopt the innovation, as distinguished from the date of installation, which followed by as much as two years; firms are ordered from early to later adopters.

name: Manager's interest in subordinates' general welfare
authors_terms: ["managers' interest in their general welfare", "manager is interested in your general welfare", "supervisory support"]
definition: The extent to which a subordinate perceives that his manager is interested in his general welfare; the authors treat this perception as the supervisory support aspect of organizational climate.

name: Perceived dependence of safety on management
authors_terms: ["think personal and organizational safety is highly dependent on the safety-related behavior of their manager", "think their personal safety and organizational safety is less dependent on the safety-related behavior of their manager", "associate safety with their manager's safety related behavior"]
definition: The extent to which subordinates believe that their personal and organizational safety depends on the safety-related behavior of their manager, reflected in the association they see between their manager's safety behavior and the safety of the work environment.

name: Manager's safety-related behavior
authors_terms: ["assessment of managers' behavior with respect to safety matters", "assessments of their manager's behavior", "managers' safety related behavior"]
definition: Subordinates' assessments of the behavior of their managers with respect to safety matters, such as directing attention toward safety practices, acting on safety requests or suggestions, and being concerned about safety.

name: Perceived safety of the work environment
authors_terms: ["your work environment is safe", "overall assessment of the safety of the work environment"]
definition: The operator's assessment of whether his work environment is safe, one of three dimensions of plant safety assessed in the study.

name: Exposure to safety hazards
authors_terms: ["exposed to safety hazards during your daily work"]
definition: The operator's assessment of the extent to which he is exposed to safety hazards during his daily work, one of three dimensions of plant safety assessed in the study.

name: Personal likelihood of an accident
authors_terms: ["you, personally, have a chance of being involved in an accident at work", "assessments of the likelihood that they personally may be involved in an accident"]
definition: The operator's assessment of the likelihood that he personally will be involved in an accident at work, one of three dimensions of plant safety assessed in the study.

name: Successor type
authors_terms: ["successor type", "inside successor", "outside successor", "promotional origin of the successor", "origin of promotion"]
definition: An inside successor is defined as a person promoted from the executive staff of the predecessor; an outside successor is anyone not in the predecessor's executive staff.

name: Leadership style
authors_terms: ["leadership style", "leadership behavior", "task oriented style", "employee oriented style", "LPC"]
definition: A large loading to the favorable side of the adjective continuums produces a high LPC score, which is indicative of an employee oriented style of leadership; the negative end of the scale forms a low LPC score, which is indicative of a task oriented leadership style.

name: Need deficiency
authors_terms: ["need deficiency", "lack of need fulfillment", "need satisfaction", "degree of need fulfillment"]
definition: The discrepancy between the amount of need a respondent perceives now and the amount he believes there should be, calculated for each of six items; positive discrepancies indicate basic satisfaction with fulfillment of needs, and negative discrepancies indicate dissatisfaction, the net value giving rise to total need satisfaction.

name: Organizational change
authors_terms: ["organizational change", "executive personnel changes", "formal administrative positional shifts", "personnel turnover"]
definition: Organizational change following succession consists of executive personnel changes and formal administrative positional shifts within the new leader's work group.

name: Environmental uncertainty
definition: The amount of environmental uncertainty facing the organization, measured by the number of major product changes made by an organization during the past five years.

name: Management system
authors_terms: ["type of management system", "organic management system", "mechanistic management system", "organic system", "mechanistic system"]
definition: The style of management of the organization, ranging from a mechanistic management system emphasizing a hierarchy of authority, specialized differentiation of functional tasks, and rules and regulations, to an organic system emphasizing lateral rather than vertical relations, participation of lower members in decision making, and greater flexibility of functional roles and relations.

name: Congruence between management system and environment
definition: The match between the type of management system and the amount of uncertainty in the organization's environment.

name: Economic success
authors_terms: ["economic success", "economic performance", "relative degree of economic success"]
definition: The economic performance of the organization, measured by percentage changes over a five-year period in sales volume in units, total unit production costs, controllable costs, and contribution to company profit, plus a subjective assessment of total organizational success.

name: Legitimate power
definition: Based on P's perception that O has a legitimate right or is officially empowered to prescribe behavior for him. In an organizational context legitimate power would be grounded in formal authority.

name: Reward power
definition: Based on P's conception that O has the ability to mediate, directly or indirectly, rewards for him. In an organization context this can include such things as O's perceived influence over promotions, salary increases, future work assignments, etc.

name: Coercive power
definition: Based on P's perception that O has the ability to mediate, directly or indirectly, penalties or punishment.

name: Expert power
definition: Based on P's perception that O has some special knowledge or expertise.

name: Friendship
definition: An influence method based on the project manager having established a personal friendship with the project person; it was included because project managers mentioned it in interviews and because it is mentioned in some of the literature on project management as a method of influence.

name: Work challenge
definition: Assigning work that the project person feels is professionally challenging. The authors argue that work challenge deals more with integrating the personal goals and needs of project personnel with project goals and is primarily oriented toward the intrinsic motivation of project personnel.

name: Project support
definition: The degree of support provided by project personnel, measured by how frequently they met the requests of their project manager with maximum effort.

name: Project involvement
definition: The degree of project involvement on the part of project personnel, covering how involved they are in their job, how often they do extra work that is not required, and how hard they feel they work in comparison with others doing the same type of work.

name: Openness of upward communication
definition: The willingness of project personnel to disagree with their project manager was used as a measure of the openness of upward communications.

name: Project performance
authors_terms: ["project performance", "effectiveness ratings of project managers", "overall effectiveness in carrying out assigned projects"]
definition: A measure of the effectiveness of the project managers obtained by asking their superiors to provide a ranking of the project managers reporting to them in terms of their overall effectiveness in carrying out assigned projects.

name: Project climate
authors_terms: ["project support, project involvement, and openness of upward communications among project personnel", "a climate of high support, disagreement, and involvement", "a climate of greater disagreement and involvement"]
definition: The authors' joint label for the level of project support, project involvement, and openness of upward communications among project personnel, referred to in the discussion as a climate of support, disagreement, and involvement among project personnel.

name: Task unit technology
authors_terms: ["task unit technology", "task unit design", "task unit (micro) technology", "the unit design"]
definition: One of four ideal types of organizational design (Routine, Engineered, Craft, and Heuristic) deduced from the interaction of task variability and personnel discretion variation; these ideal types can be considered either as task units or as entire organizations depending upon which unit of analysis one chooses to use.

name: Modal organization technology
authors_terms: ["modal technology", "modal organizational technology", "modal (macro) level", "primary production modality"]
definition: The aggregated technology of a plant's primary production subsystem, i.e., the direct and indirect labor groups, as opposed to the technology of individual task units; an index of modal technology was generated from the company's job code classification as reported by each department manager.

name: Management autonomy
authors_terms: ["autonomy", "decision autonomy", "decision making discretion", "autonomy structure", "perceptions of autonomy", "authority, control, and autonomy"]
definition: The relationships between each task unit and the administration system and between task unit members and task unit supervision, with the concepts of autonomy, authority, and control providing the common fabric; these relationships can be expressed in terms of a manager's autonomy.

name: Hierarchical level
authors_terms: ["hierarchy", "level of management", "hierarchical level", "first and second level managers"]
definition: The level of management in the hierarchy; the study distinguishes first level managers (supervisors and project leaders) from second level managers (managers of first level managers).

name: Total amount of control
authors_terms: ["total control", "total amount of control", "amount of total control"]
definition: The total amount of control represented by the height of the control curve; it is operationalized as the sum of the three points which make up the control curve.

name: Distribution of control
authors_terms: ["distribution of control", "slope of the control curve"]
definition: The distribution of control represented by the slope of the control curve, visualized as distributed along a continuum with the extremes termed autocratic and democratic management systems.

name: Concordance
definition: Concordance is defined as the degree of agreement among hierarchical echelons' perceptions of the organizational control structure, operationalized by measuring the extent to which control curves constructed for each organizational level coincide.

name: Organizational effectiveness
definition: Organizational effectiveness defined largely in terms of members' satisfactions and some production indicators; in this study it is measured by ten criterion dependent variables derived from items tapping relevant aspects of satisfaction and organizational functioning.

name: Task unit design
authors_terms: ["task unit design", "structural design", "organizational strategy", "task unit design types", "Matrix cells"]
definition: Each of the Perrow and Matrix models offers one of four ideal types of organizational design or strategy, which can be considered as task units or as entire organizations. Alternative task unit or organization designs are appropriate, given variation in task variability and personnel discretion.

name: Task unit autonomy
authors_terms: ["autonomy of the work group (task unit) vis-a-vis the overall organization (administrative system)", "task-unit autonomy", "autonomy from the administrative system"]
definition: The autonomy of the work group (task unit) vis-a-vis the overall organization (administrative system), akin to the authority structure dimension of organization.

name: Task unit member autonomy
authors_terms: ["autonomy that exists within the task unit between the unit member and the unit leader", "task unit member autonomy", "autonomy from the task unit supervisor"]
definition: The autonomy that exists within the task unit between the unit member and the unit leader or relative to job definitions, resembling aspects of the participative management literature.

name: Centralization of the personnel function
authors_terms: ["centralized personnel function", "centralization of the personnel function", "centralization"]
definition: The personnel function, or personnel administration, is the totality of concern with the human resources of organization; the centralized personnel function applies the previous definition plus the condition that at least two-thirds of the total state employees must be serviced in a single bureau of the state government.

name: Comprehensive merit system
definition: A personnel system in which comparative merit or ability governs each individual's selection and progress in the service, and in which the conditions and rewards of performance contribute to the competency and continuity of the service; for the comprehensive merit system at least two-thirds of the total state employees are covered under such a system.

name: Urbanization of the state
definition: An urban state is defined as a state in which the population proportion living in urban areas is 60 per cent or greater; a rural state is defined as a state in which the population proportion living in rural areas is 40 per cent or greater.

name: Unionization of state employees
authors_terms: ["employee organizations", "employees organized for collective bargaining purposes", "unionization", "large numbers of employees"]
definition: Employee organizations are formally organized employee groups, formed for collective bargaining about those conditions of employment on which state law permits negotiation; these organizations need not be trade unions as such. Large numbers of employees in employee organizations are defined as at least one-third of the state's total employment.

name: Interorganizational conflict
definition: The first variable, interorganizational conflict, is viewed as varying from high levels to low levels of conflict relations between two organizations, and is looked upon as a special case of lateral intergroup conflict between separate yet functionally interdependent units connected along the flow of work.

name: Interorganizational linking process
definition: Linkage or interorganizational linking process (ILP) refers to the communication, balance, and decision-making engaged in by salesmen; it indicates the process of interorganizational coordination and varies from high frequency to low frequency.

name: Interorganizational exchange
definition: Exchange refers to those material and non-material interactions between organizations that have an effect upon their goals; it is ordered from high to low and indicates the effectiveness of interorganization management.

name: Number of organization levels
authors_terms: ["number of levels in an organization", "organization levels", "the number of levels", "organization structures", "levels"]
definition: The number of hierarchical levels in the organization structure; the experimental organizations had two, three, or four levels.

name: Profitability
authors_terms: ["profit measure of performance", "goal of profitability", "percentage return on sales", "profit per decision", "total accumulated profit"]
definition: Each organization measured its performance primarily by its goal of profitability, and this was measured in terms of a percentage return on sales.

name: Communication time
authors_terms: ["time to a decision", "time per decision", "communication efficiency", "the time required to reach a decision in each trial"]
definition: Communication efficiency measured by the time required to reach a decision in each trial.

name: Errors
authors_terms: ["error measure of performance", "number of errors", "errors per decision", "communication accuracy"]
definition: Communication efficiency measured by the number of errors made in each trial.

name: Individual attitudes toward the organization
authors_terms: ["individual member attitudes", "individual's attitudes toward the organization", "individual satisfaction", "satisfaction with organizational role"]
definition: Attitudes measured by a questionnaire designed to measure the overall satisfaction of the subjects based on his perceptions of his organizational role, the organization performance, and his role in the decision process.

name: Game performance
definition: A composite score built from numerically weighted points awarded for six business objectives — share of the market, inventory, cash, profit, owners' equity, and dividends. The total of these values is referred to as the game performance score and serves as the criterion variable of the study.

name: All-college GPA
definition: All-College GPA is the average grade point for all of the game player's college work.

name: All-business GPA
definition: The All-Business GPA refers to the average grade point for all courses that have a business prefix in the university catalog.

name: All-quantitative GPA
definition: The All-Quantitative GPA is the average grade point for all courses taken in which quantitative techniques are used extensively - for example, courses in mathematics, statistics, operations research.

name: Achievement
definition: One of the attributes measured by the Edwards Personal Preference Schedule that the authors predict will correlate positively with game performance; no further definition is given in the text.

name: Dominance
definition: An attribute measured by the Edwards Personal Preference Schedule, predicted to correlate positively with game performance and described as indicating a strong need to be a leader among one's peers and to influence and direct the actions of others.

name: Intraception
definition: One of the attributes measured by the Edwards Personal Preference Schedule that the authors predict will correlate positively with game performance; no further definition is given in the text.

name: Nurturance
definition: One of the attributes measured by the Edwards Personal Preference Schedule that the authors predict will correlate negatively with game performance; no further definition is given in the text.

name: Abasement
definition: One of the attributes measured by the Edwards Personal Preference Schedule that the authors predict will correlate negatively with game performance; no further definition is given in the text.

name: Succorance
definition: One of the attributes measured by the Edwards Personal Preference Schedule that the authors predict will correlate negatively with game performance; no further definition is given in the text.

name: Supervisory ability
definition: One of the managerial attributes measured by the Ghiselli Self-Description Inventory, predicted to relate positively to game performance; no further definition is given in the text.

name: Intelligence
definition: One of the managerial attributes measured by the Ghiselli Self-Description Inventory, predicted to relate positively to game performance; no further definition is given in the text.

name: Self-assurance
definition: One of the managerial attributes measured by the Ghiselli Self-Description Inventory, predicted to relate positively to game performance; no further definition is given in the text.

name: Decision-making ability
definition: One of the managerial attributes measured by the Ghiselli Self-Description Inventory, predicted to relate positively to game performance; no further definition is given in the text.

name: Perceived occupational level
definition: One of the managerial attributes measured by the Ghiselli Self-Description Inventory, predicted to relate positively to game performance; no further definition is given in the text.

name: Initiative
definition: One of the managerial attributes measured by the Ghiselli Self-Description Inventory, predicted to relate positively to game performance; no further definition is given in the text.

name: Vocabulary
definition: An attribute measured in the business study by the Miner Short Vocabulary Test and compared with game performance; no further definition is given in the text.

name: Founder gender
definition: Our primary explanatory variable indicates whether a startup was female- or male-led; for team-founded startups, founders' gender was classified based on the individual designated as the 'primary contact,' typically the CEO, who led the pitch and interacted most with judges.

name: Selection at the shortlisting stage
definition: The shortlisting stage outcome: evaluators make less-binding, lower-stakes selections (e.g., inviting candidates for interviews, sending grant proposals out for review) that will be revisited at a later stage before more-substantial commitments are made.

name: Selection at the winners stage
definition: The winners stage outcome: evaluators make more-binding commitments by making decisions about candidates that are more difficult to reverse, allocating the ultimate resource that the evaluation process is designed to distribute.

name: Assessed startup quality
definition: Each judge independently rated each startup's overall quality on a 0 to 5 scale, indicating whether it should be selected, from 0 (''definitely don't recommend'') to 5 (''definitely recommend'').

name: Conceptual distance from competitors
definition: A text-based measure of how differentiated each startup was from its competition, calculated as the average cosine distance between each startup's written description and that of all other startups in the same industry-year.

name: Funding awarded to winners
definition: Winners could receive up to $100,000 in equity-free funding according to their ratings by judges, and winners that scored more highly were allocated more funding than others.

name: Startup survival
definition: Long-term survival measured by tracking how long each startup's website remained active from the competition date, assuming that website shutdown typically coincides with business closure.

name: State-owned enterprise density
authors_terms: ["SOE density", "density of SOEs", "density of the SOE population"]
definition: The total number of state-owned enterprises of a particular form operating in any given year, counted within an industry at the three-digit SIC level and including both firms in the sample and firms established before 1998.

name: Collectively owned enterprise density
authors_terms: ["COE density", "density of COEs", "density of the COE population"]
definition: The total number of collectively owned enterprises operating in any given year, counted within an industry at the three-digit SIC level and including both firms in the sample and firms established before 1998.

name: Privately owned enterprise density
authors_terms: ["POE density", "density of POEs", "density of the POE population"]
definition: The total number of privately owned enterprises (private, limited liability and shareholding firms) operating in any given year, counted within an industry at the three-digit SIC level and including both firms in the sample and firms established before 1998.

name: State-owned enterprise exit rate
definition: The rate at which state-owned enterprises leave the population covered by the annual census; exit is coded when a focal firm at time t did not exist in the database at time t + 1.

name: Collectively owned enterprise exit rate
definition: The rate at which collectively owned enterprises leave the population covered by the annual census; exit is coded when a focal firm at time t did not exist in the database at time t + 1.

name: Privately owned enterprise exit rate
definition: The rate at which privately owned enterprises leave the population covered by the annual census; exit is coded when a focal firm at time t did not exist in the database at time t + 1.

name: Label ambiguity
definition: The extent to which a label's boundaries are unclear; when members of a label primarily identify elsewhere, the focal label is less likely to develop a shared social meaning, and fuzziness measures the extent to which members of a label identify elsewhere.

name: Label spanning
authors_terms: ["label spanning", "number of labels organization claims", "organization-level ambiguity"]
definition: The number of market labels the organization claims in a given year, which is ambiguity that arises from generalism at the organization level.

name: Consumer evaluation
definition: How appealing a software company is to consumers, who purchase the offerings; because rank in the Software 500 is based on software revenues, it indicates how appealing a software company is to consumers.

name: Venture capitalist evaluation
definition: Venture capitalist evaluations were measured in terms of whether a company received venture capital funding in a given year.

name: Client defection
definition: The event of interest was the defection of clients from Arthur Andersen, and the dependent variable is the unobserved hazard rate of defection.

name: Institutional ownership concentration
authors_terms: ["institutional ownership concentration", "institutional ownership", "public pension fund ownership"]
definition: Institutional ownership is a binary variable coded one if public pension funds holding at least $100 million in equity assets, such as the California Public Employee Retirement System (CalPERS), together owned more than 5 percent of the shares in a firm, which would allow them as a group to put pressure on management.

name: Security analyst coverage
definition: A firm is therefore 'covered' by security analysts when at least one analyst working for an investment bank or a brokerage house monitors the firm, regularly forecasts its earnings, and makes investment recommendations.

name: Stock exchange listing
definition: Though all publicly traded firms have to abide by Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) rules and regulations, the stock exchanges of some firms expose them to tougher regulatory environments. The New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) traditionally has been viewed as the exchange with the toughest listing requirements.

name: Media coverage of prior defections
authors_terms: ["media coverage", "defection articles", "media coverage of prior defections"]
definition: The business press is typically the first source of information about dramatic business events for the vast majority of firms not directly involved in the events. As defections began accumulating, the media ensured that knowledge about these defections was widely disseminated.

name: Defections by large firms
authors_terms: ["prior defections of large firms", "defections of large firms", "Fortune 500 defections"]
definition: For the compromised high-status partner, the defection of large firms represents a threat to its survival because of their sizable audit fees and the loss of status associated with their defection.

name: Board interlock with defectors
definition: When firms are interlocked with prior adopters through shared directors, these directors can bring their experiences to bear on their focal board, thus increasing directors' awareness of the particular issue as well as their knowledge about how to deal with it.

name: Commitment to audit quality
authors_terms: ["commitment to quality", "abnormal audit fee", "higher-than-expected audit fees", "audit fees"]
definition: The willingness to pay extra for a high-status partner is an indicator of how important quality is to firms. When firms are willing to pay higher audit fees than should be expected given the risk and complexity of their businesses, however, they likely have strong commitments to audit quality.

name: Competitive inertia
definition: Competitive inertia refers to the level of activity that a firm demonstrates in altering its competitive stand; it reflects the number of market-oriented changes a company makes in trying to attract customers and outmaneuver competitors. Inertia is said to be high when, relative to rivals of similar scale, companies make few changes in competitive practices.

name: Performance
authors_terms: ["performance", "operating revenue per available seat mile", "revenue per available seat mile", "R/ASM"]
definition: Performance was measured by operating revenue per available seat mile flown: R/ASM. This index reflects not only the load factor of an airline but also the revenue produced thereby.

name: Market diversity
definition: Market diversity exposes the organization to a great variety of ideas and events, some of which may prompt exploration and change; it is a diverse market environment with many different kinds of customers and competitors. Market diversity was measured by a composite index assessing the number of different airports served by each airline and the number of competitors faced by each airline.

name: Market growth
authors_terms: ["market growth", "market decline", "growing market", "total industry business volume"]
definition: Market growth was measured by the level of growth in total industry business volume, an indicator of the degree to which new markets or niches are opening up. This was assessed by the annual change in total revenue passenger miles for the entire domestic airline passenger business.

name: Competitive experience
authors_terms: ["competitive experience", "breadth of competitive experience", "past repertoire of actions", "level of recent competitive activity"]
definition: One key aspect of managers' past experience is the past repertoire of actions that an organization has used; a company's breadth of competitive experience was assessed as competitive inertia during the previous year, providing an overall assessment of a company's level of activity in the past.

name: Firm age
definition: Firm age was measured in years.

name: Firm size
definition: Size was simply the natural log of the number of full-time employees.

name: CEO tenure
authors_terms: ["tenure", "length of tenure of the incumbent CEO", "CEO tenure"]
definition: Tenure measures the number of years the incumbent has served as CEO and is used as the duration measure in all models estimated.

name: Economic adversity
definition: Poor economic performance, which political theories of organizations see as a triggering device for executive turnover and which the authors treat as the condition under which latent political contests become manifest.

name: Prior board tenure
authors_terms: ["prior board tenure", "prior board experience", "prior board tenure of the incumbent CEO"]
definition: Prior board tenure measures the experience the CEO has had with the board before assuming the top executive position, measured as the number of years of the CEO's board tenure before first becoming CEO.

name: Proportion of CEO-appointed directors
authors_terms: ["CEO appointees", "proportion of directors appointed during the CEO's incumbency", "proportion of his board appointments"]
definition: The proportion of all directors first appointed during the CEO's incumbency; the CEO's power becomes more entrenched as the proportion of his board appointments increases.

name: Proportion of outside directors
definition: The number of outside board members divided by the total number of directors; outsiders are seen as independent from the influence of the CEO and able to limit his power.

name: Board size
authors_terms: ["board size", "number of directors", "size of the board"]
definition: Board size measured the number of board members, both insider directors and outside directors; a large board is more likely than a small one to generate alternative political coalitions that challenge the CEO.

name: Separation of chairman and CEO positions
authors_terms: ["separate chairman", "separation of the position of chairman of the board and of CEO", "chairman"]
definition: The separation of the position of chairman of the board from that of CEO; a separate chairman is more likely to monitor the interests of the shareholders and is a natural candidate for the organization of a political coalition opposed to the CEO.

name: CEO succession rate
authors_terms: ["CEO succession", "rate of CEO succession", "rate of executive succession"]
definition: CEO succession events were coded from Standard and Poor's Directory of Corporations, Officers, and Directors based on changes in the names of the relevant officers; all hypotheses are presented in terms of their effects on the rate of CEO succession.

name: Dependence
authors_terms: ["dependence", "constraining dependencies", "dependence relations", "level of dependence", "direct dependence", "two-step dependence"]
definition: The dependence network defines the relations that are expected to generate cooptive responses. Using path distances, and assuming that constraint is a negative function of the number of steps between ego and alter, four levels of dependence were defined.

name: Direct cooptation
definition: The direct form occurs when A limits him- or herself to an embedded relationship with B and avoids cooptive ties with C. Because coordination between two actors may curtail the autonomy of a limiting party, a strategic option for the dependent player is to gain leverage over a limiting party by coopting actors who constrain this party.

name: Two-step cooptation
authors_terms: ["two-step leverage", "two-step cooptive ties", "two-step form", "two-step maneuvers", "two-step strategies"]
definition: The two-step form occurs when the strategic player (A) avoids the limiting party (B) and builds cooptive ties with someone who constrains this party's performance (C). In this case, the indirect strategy substitutes for direct cooptation.

name: Conflict
definition: In organizational settings, conflictive dependencies may arise for a variety of reasons, from the clash between opposite interests or views on organizational policies to simple interpersonal conflict. Ties were coded as conflictive if either ego or alter cited the other party as someone who had troubled him or her in the performance of his or her role or as someone whose influence on a key issue he or she actively tried to neutralize.

name: Internalization of R&D
authors_terms: ["internalize R&D", "in-house R&D", "vertically integrate", "internal R&D procurement", "backward vertical integration from marketing to R&D"]
definition: The pharmaceutical firm's choice of undertaking an R&D project through in-house or collaborative modes, i.e., whether it develops the required R&D capabilities in-house (vertically integrates) or procures the necessary R&D services from a new biotechnology firm.

name: Small-numbers bargaining hazard
authors_terms: ["small-numbers-bargaining hazards", "small-numbers-bargaining problem", "concentration of R&D suppliers", "specialized R&D capabilities"]
definition: A hazard that arises when a firm investing in transaction-specific assets has limited exchange alternatives, because such assets limit its ability to switch partners and make it vulnerable to opportunistic recontracting. In R&D procurement it depends on the degree to which the know-how being procured is specialized to the supplier, i.e., on the number of R&D suppliers with programmes in the product application area.

name: Product market rivalry
authors_terms: ["rivalry", "competition from other established pharmaceutical companies", "product-market rivalry", "competition in product markets"]
definition: The number of established pharmaceutical companies attempting to develop or commercialize the same product or other products within the same area of therapeutic application. Each rival competing in the same therapeutic market represents a possible buyer for the technology a contractor might expropriate, so greater rivalry creates an incentive to internalize.

name: Historical R&D procurement pattern
authors_terms: ["historical propensity to procure R&D internally", "historical pattern of R&D procurement", "historical R&D procurement patterns"]
definition: A firm's historical pattern of obtaining product R&D from its own laboratories rather than external sources, which reflects deeply engrained repertoires, search rules, operating procedures and routines. Firms lacking experience with R&D contracting are likely to be less able to search for and select R&D partners and to absorb technologies from external sources.

name: R&D experience in the relevant technology
authors_terms: ["biotechnology R&D experience", "prior R&D experience", "accumulated in-house R&D experience", "R&D learning curve"]
definition: The firm's prior in-house R&D experience in the technological area in which a project is conducted. Because technical advance is cumulative, the know-how needed to innovate at time t+1 depends on what is learned during R&D at time t, so prior experience reduces the costs of internalizing new projects.

name: Dependence on the pharmaceutical business
authors_terms: ["focus", "percentage of its business in pharmaceuticals", "dependence on the pharmaceutical business", "percentage of each firm's total sales attributable to its pharmaceutical business"]
definition: The size of the pharmaceutical business relative to the other businesses managed by the corporation, which affects whether corporate management views biopharmaceutical technology as strategically important and allocates the resources required for internalization.

name: Firm size
definition: The size of the firm measured in pharmaceutical sales; the authors note that theory does not provide unambiguous prior expectations about its effect on R&D boundaries, because larger firms may have scale-economy advantages while increasing size also adds complexity to the administrative process.

name: Japanese national context
definition: The distinction between manufacturing plants located in Japan and plants located in the United States; the authors compare the two national samples on levels of structural properties and on the effects of task contingencies.

name: Functional specialization
authors_terms: ["functional specialization", "specialization of employees' work roles", "division of labor"]
definition: The specificity and definition of individuals' work roles; employees in Japanese organizations are expected to be generalists performing a range of job functions. Measured as the proportion of functions assigned to individuals as full-time responsibilities.

name: Subunit differentiation
authors_terms: ["differentiation of collective subunits", "departments and sections", "subunit differentiation"]
definition: The proliferation of collective units such as departments and sections below the plant manager; Japanese organizations are described as elaborately and minutely divided into separate and distinct organizational units.

name: Vertical differentiation
authors_terms: ["vertical differentiation", "number of levels of authority/status", "authority levels", "ranks"]
definition: The number of hierarchical levels from the lowest direct worker to the highest manager in the plant; Japanese hierarchies are described as tall and finely graded.

name: Span of control
definition: The number of subordinates reporting to a manager, measured for the plant manager and for the average first-line supervisor.

name: Managerial proportion
authors_terms: ["percentage of managers", "ratio of managers to total employees", "management component"]
definition: The share of a plant's employees who are managers rather than direct production workers; the belief that Japanese companies have a higher percentage of employees above the rank of direct worker follows from the nenko promotion system.

name: Centralization of formal authority
definition: The hierarchical level at which the formal authority to make decisions resides, averaged over the decision items; higher values indicate that formal authority rests at higher organizational levels, i.e., less delegation.

name: Centralization of de facto decision making
authors_terms: ["centralization of de facto decision making", "de facto responsibility", "actual decision-making involvement"]
definition: The hierarchical level at which decisions are in practice usually made, averaged over the decision items; higher values indicate that decisions are actually made at higher organizational levels.

name: Formalization
definition: The codification of procedures in written form, with procedures heavily codified, files and record-keeping abounding, and written communications proliferating.

name: Ringi
definition: The circulation of formal proposals for the purpose of obtaining seals of approval by affected managers and departments; through ringi Japanese organizations seek wide participation in each decision and defer final action until consensus is reached.

name: Quality circle activity
definition: Small-group programs at the direct production level that are viewed as structures for eliciting participation in decisions or as methods of diffusing responsibility and building consensus.

name: Operations technology
definition: The production technology of the plant, measured by the Woodward classification of custom/small batch, large batch/mass production and continuous process, the Amber-Amber automation scale, and the Aston workflow rigidity scale.

name: Environmental munificence
definition: Environmental munificence is the extent to which the environment can support sustained growth, and it is quite similar to Aldrich's concept of environmental capacity; organizations seek out environments that permit organizational growth and stability.

name: Environmental complexity
definition: Environmental complexity is the heterogeneity of and range of an organization's activities; organizations competing in industries that require many different inputs or produce many different outputs should find resource acquisition or disposal of output more complex.

name: Environmental dynamism
definition: Dynamism is restricted to change that is hard to predict and that heightens uncertainty for key organizational members; turnover, absence of pattern, and unpredictability are the best measures of environmental stability-instability.

name: Technical innovation adoption
authors_terms: ["technical innovations", "rate of adoption of technical innovations"]
definition: Technical innovations are defined as innovations that occur in the technical system of an organization and are directly related to the primary work activity of the organization. A technical innovation can be the implementation of an idea for a new product or a new service or the introduction of new elements in an organization's production process or service operation.

name: Administrative innovation adoption
authors_terms: ["administrative innovations", "rate of adoption of administrative innovations"]
definition: Administrative innovations are defined as those that occur in the social system of an organization, which refers to the relationships among people who interact to accomplish a particular goal or task. An administrative innovation can be the implementation of a new way to recruit personnel, allocate resources, and structure tasks, authority, and rewards.

name: Organizational lag
