definition: The concept of organizational lag, the "discrepancy in the rate at which new technical and administrative ideas are implemented in an organization" (Evan, 1966: 52), was used to study the relationship between technical and administrative innovations and the possible impact of their rate of adoption on an organization's performance.

name: Organizational performance
definition: From a systems perspective, performance is the ability of an organization to cope with all four systemic processes (inputs, outputs, transformations, and feedback effects) relative to its goal-seeking behavior (Evan, 1976). A high-performing organization would accomplish its primary tasks efficiently and would carry out its organization-maintaining and organization-adapting functions effectively.

name: Resource dependence
authors_terms: ["resource dependence", "perceived dependence on others for resources", "perceptions of dependence", "perceived need for resources"]
definition: An organization's perceived dependence on other organizations to obtain resources, which compels it to become involved in an interorganizational relationship; the authors state that 'the roots of interorganizational activity are internal to each organization' and that IR's are largely stimulated by perceptions of need for resources from other organizations.

name: Domain similarity
definition: The degree to which organizations have the same services, clients, and personnel skills.

name: Communications
authors_terms: ["communications", "communication frequency", "frequent communications", "written communications and phone calls"]
definition: Contacts between the parties to a relationship; the authors view communication as an 'adjustment process' through which individuals collectively shape their relationship.

name: Formalization
definition: The extent to which the agreement establishing the relationship is written and legally binding, specifying the contractual terms of the interorganizational relationship.

name: Consensus
definition: Agreement among the parties on the goals and methods of their relationship; the authors write that in the process of communication 'one's agreement with and trust in another are transformed over time into collective phenomena of consensus.'

name: Monetary transactions
definition: The exchange of financial resources between organizations, which was basic to the survival of the ECD organizations and one of the two most important kinds of resources they needed to sustain ongoing operations.

name: Client referrals
definition: The referral of clients (children, patients, or families) from one organization to another for services; the second major resource the ECD organizations needed to operate on an ongoing basis.

name: Monitoring
definition: The funding agency's procedures for ensuring that the terms of an agreement are adhered to, including requirements that the recipient submit periodic fiscal and performance reports and that funding agency representatives make periodic site visits.

name: Norms of equity
definition: The degree to which each organizational party judges that the other fulfills its commitments and that the relationship is worthwhile, equitable, productive, and satisfying.

name: Internal labor market arrangements
authors_terms: ["internal labor market (ILM)", "firm internal labor market (FILM)", "ILM arrangements"]
definition: An administrative unit where pricing, allocation, and training decisions are governed by a set of administrative rules and procedures and not merely by the economic forces of the external labor market. The authors adopt the emphasis on allocation of labor as the primary defining characteristic of the FILM and focus primarily on hiring and promotion.

name: Firm-specific skills
definition: Employees with firm-specific training are valuable to the organization and their turnover is costly, because a new employee would have to receive comparable training before performing at the same level; specific training raises the value of the worker to the employer but not the wage the worker could command in the external labor market. There was no direct information on the extent to which establishments employed workers with firm-specific skills, so the training provided was used to index various degrees of skill specificity.

name: Technological change
definition: Changes in the establishment's plant, equipment, internal operating procedures, work arrangements, and materials used in the production process, which are hypothesized to make the technology and hence the workers' skills more idiosyncratic.

name: Core sector location
authors_terms: ["core sector", "location in the dual economy", "industrial sector"]
definition: The organization's location in the dual economy, particularly whether it is in the industrial core or at the periphery.

name: Government organization
definition: Whether the establishment is part of the government; services provided by governmental bureaucracies are said to be more difficult to evaluate than those provided by many other types of organizations, making them likely contexts for institutionalized practices.

name: Personnel department
definition: A personnel department is an organizational arrangement hypothesized to be positively associated with having an FILM: it signals emphasis on legitimate human resource management activities, is functionally interrelated with career ladders, and provides an internal constituency interested in having an ILM as a professionally sanctioned practice.

name: Unionization
authors_terms: ["unionization", "extent of unionization of the workers", "percentage of employees covered by a collective bargaining agreement"]
definition: The presence and strength of a union in the organization, measured by the percentage of employees covered by a collective bargaining agreement.

name: Labor scarcity
definition: The extent to which an organization has problems securing an adequate supply of labor; organizations are likely to take action to manage critical resources when they are difficult to obtain, and an ILM can induce workers to stay and bind them to the organization.

name: Establishment size
definition: The number of employees in the establishment, measured by the natural logarithm of the number of employees in 1967.

name: Change in establishment size
definition: Whether the establishment's size has been increasing or decreasing; growth increases promotion opportunities and makes an ILM more likely, while declining size makes operating an ILM more difficult.

name: Branch establishment
definition: Whether the establishment is a branch site rather than a single site or headquarters; being a branch may make promotional opportunities more available and may proxy for total firm size.

name: Self-serving attributions
definition: Self-serving attributional patterns are usually manifested in the justification of organizational performance by a tendency to associate positive events to internal causes and negative events to external ones. Self-serving attributions are a specific instance of causal reasoning that allows the writer to take credit for good news and avoid blame for bad news.

name: Organizational performance
definition: Net income was chosen as a proxy for performance due to its focus on shareholders, who are remunerated according to it. It is also the proxy for performance that is easiest for an investor to understand.

name: Capital market context
definition: Contextual events, in the form of mixed combinations of good (bad) year and high (low) performers, are assumed to exert influence on the relative weights of motivational and informational drivers in the process of justification of organizational performance. In order to provide variation in the context variable within the sample, a good year and a bad year were selected using the per capita gross domestic product and the Ibovespa (Bovespa index) as proxies.

name: Competition among member organizations
definition: The degree of rivalry among the target organizations of the cartel in the market for athletic talent and gate receipts. In a competitive situation, success is a fixed-sum proposition, especially if competitors play relatively closed schedules.

name: Detection of rule violations
authors_terms: ["probability of detection for a rule violation", "detected violations", "sanctions received", "probability of being penalized"]
definition: The probability that a rule violation is detected and penalized. Enforcement machinery operates when a complaint is filed by a member institution, athlete, or other interested party, so surveillance is carried out by one competitor reporting another's violations.

name: Threat to cartel stability
authors_terms: ["threat to the stability of the cartel", "visibility", "athletic prestige", "national ranking"]
definition: The viability of the control agreement will be threatened by actions of any party that would provide either a permanent advantage, reducing dependency on the cartel, or promoting outside intervention; the public visibility of a particular rule violator is an incentive for careful cartel control.

name: Sanction severity
authors_terms: ["severity of penalties", "severity of sanctions", "level of sanction"]
definition: The severity of the punishment administered by the control agent. Actual penalties are designed to restore or maintain competitive position, and were ranked in order of severity according to the NCAA sanctioning procedure.

name: Type of rule violation
authors_terms: ["nature of rule violations", "types of violations", "aid-related infractions", "nonaid-related infractions"]
definition: Infractions were classified into 23 specific categories, which were then more generally classified as aid-related or nonaid-related; aid-related infractions indicated violations of the basic recruiting regulations.

name: Change in organizational performance
authors_terms: ["relative changes in the level of organizational performance", "sudden change in performance", "improved performance", "declining performance"]
definition: Year-to-year alteration in an organization's competitive success. The one basis on which the performance of major competitors is directly comparable is the national ranking system.

name: Dependence on the association
authors_terms: ["dependence upon the cartel", "dependence upon the association", "dependency on the cartel"]
definition: Organizations that are most dependent upon the cartel are least able to withdraw when punishment is meted out; institutions that depend on either athletic income or athletic prestige, which is mediated by the cartel, are most vulnerable to its discipline.

name: Agency power relative to United Way
definition: Power is usually defined as the capacity to control others; power does not have to be exercised to exist, and there is a distinct difference between the capacity to control and actual performance of control.

name: Potential power
definition: Power relationships may exist even though no immediate outcome is evident or no obvious power attempt has been made; such relations are based on potential power, and dependence is an indicator of potential rather than enacted power.

name: Enacted power
definition: If actor B is complying with the expressed wishes of actor A, we typically assume that A is exercising power over B; enacted power is the actual performance of control.

name: Perceived power
definition: Respondents are asked how much power one party has over another; they tend to base their judgments not only on the outcomes of specific power attempts they have witnessed, but also on how much power they infer one party has over the other from other behaviors and sources of information.

name: Links to the community through individuals
authors_terms: ["links to the community through interested individuals", "links with individuals"]
definition: Agencies maintain ties to the community through the individuals affiliated with them — employees, volunteers and clients — all of whom have an interest in seeing the services of the agency continue and prosper and thus have a stake in its receiving financial support from United Way.

name: Links to the community through elites
authors_terms: ["links to the community through elite individuals", "links with elites"]
definition: Ties to community elites are maintained through membership on the agencies' boards of directors; cooptation of elite or otherwise influential members of the community is a well-documented way for organizations to gain power.

name: Interorganizational linkages
definition: An organization can acquire power by developing linkages with other organizations; human service agencies commonly develop these linkages by engaging in joint programs with other agencies or by having board members who also serve on the boards of other organizations, including interlocks with the United Way board.

name: Establishment in domain
definition: Human service organizations that have existed continuously within a community for a long period have demonstrated their ability to maintain and defend a domain that provides them with the resources needed for survival, and their secure establishment can be used as a source of power relative to United Way.

name: Demand for services
definition: In the absence of criteria to judge effectiveness, community need for services could become a more important criterion for the funding of social service agencies, and available statistics on client groups are likely to be used to provide rough indicators of demand for services.

name: Service intensity
definition: Agencies differ in the intensity of the services they provide: some provide relatively limited services to large numbers of clients, while others provide intensive and comprehensive services to a smaller number of clients; agencies with high costs per client are likely to be involved in relatively intensive and comprehensive services.

name: Environmental linkages
authors_terms: ["linkages with elements of the community", "links with important community elements", "linkages to the larger environment", "environmental linkages"]
definition: Links maintained by organizations to the larger environment upon which both they and their resource suppliers may be dependent; interorganizational power can best be understood by examining linkages between organizations and their larger environment, and organizations maintaining extensive linkages to this larger environment are most likely to be powerful within their organizational network.

name: Distinctive competence
definition: Those things that an organization does especially well in comparison to its competitors; it is an aggregate of numerous specific activities that the organization tends to perform better than other organizations within a similar environment.

name: Organizational strategy
authors_terms: ["organizational strategy", "strategy type", "Defender strategy", "Prospector strategy", "Analyzer strategy", "Reactor strategy"]
definition: The strategic orientation of an organization, characterized by the Miles and Snow (1978) typology, which is the only typology that characterizes an organization as a complete system, especially its strategic orientation.

name: Organizational performance
definition: Organizational performance, or effectiveness, is a multifaceted phenomenon that is difficult to comprehend and measure; in this study an objective measure of profitability was used as a surrogate of overall organizational performance.

name: Strategy distribution
authors_terms: ["distribution of perceived strategies", "strategies perceived by top managers"]
definition: The pattern of the four organizational strategies perceived by top managers within an industry, both the relative numerical frequency of each strategy type and its incidence across industries.

name: Paradigm development
definition: The degree to which a scientific field is characterized by agreement over theory, methodology, and the content of the field; highly developed paradigms represent high consensus.

name: Departmental size
definition: The size of the department, measured as the average number of full-time-equivalent regular faculty.

name: Faculty seniority mix
authors_terms: ["seniority mix", "faculty seniority mix", "demography of the department"]
definition: The distribution of the rank and length of service of the faculty members in the department.

name: Departmental growth
authors_terms: ["growth", "growth in the proportion of regular faculty"]
definition: Growth in resources, used as an indicator of success in public organizations, measured as the change in the proportion of total faculty by department.

name: Average tenure of department heads
definition: Average length of time department heads serve in office in a department, computed by dividing the length of the period by the number of heads who served during the period.

name: Resource scarcity
definition: The condition of resource availability prevailing in the environment, with the second ten-year period being one of greatly increased financial stringency and campus political turmoil.

name: Work motifs
definition: For a given firm, work motifs reflect the intellectual ethos or prevailing set of ideas concerning what architecture is and what it should accomplish. Motifs relate to the explicit cognitive orientations that architects in a particular firm share.

name: Organizational innovation
definition: Successful innovation is the firm's success in winning design awards; firms that are successful in innovative design can be distinguished from firms that have settled for less original, more routine architectural work.

name: Structural complexity
definition: Structural differentiation is conventionally measured by the total number of units under the top executive, distinguishing major divisions responsible for basic operations from small support units.

name: Task diversity
definition: Complexity is also conceptualized in terms of how numerous are the tasks that refer to different kinds of operations and activities.

name: Environmental complexity
definition: Three variables indicate environmental complexity — nonprivate clients, joint ventures, and use of consultants.

name: Organizational size
definition: As conventionally measured, size is the number of full-time equivalent staff.

name: Computer use
definition: Technology is indicated by whether or not the staff had access to a computer. In architectural firms a computer tends to be used for many functions besides administration.

name: Written rules
definition: The extent to which operating procedures are embodied in written rules indicates the degree of formalization; formalization is viewed as a form of constraint.

name: Impersonal recruitment
definition: Impersonal recruitment is a formal and standardized procedure in which junior architects are selected through advertising in newspapers or professional journals rather than through networks of colleagues.

name: Organizational structure
definition: The structural properties of a population of organizations within industrial categories that the study predicts: the degree of bureaucratization and the development of professional staff. These two structural ratios are given for selected Canadian and American industrial sectors.

name: Bureaucratization
definition: Operationally defined as clerical personnel as a percentage of all administrative staff. The clerical-administrative ratio is taken by organizational analysts as an index of bureaucracy because it indicates such central bureaucratic processes as the diffusion and use of rules and standard operating procedures, the transmission, filing, and storage of information, differentiation, and hierarchical control.

name: Professionalization
authors_terms: ["professionalization", "development of professional staff", "staff or professional structures", "professionals as % authority"]
definition: An index showing the development of staff or professional structures, measured by professional personnel as a percentage of the authority structure. Professional expertise is in many ways an alternative to bureaucratic organizational behavior and structure.

name: Industry founding era
authors_terms: ["age of industry", "period of origin", "period of development", "prefactory", "early nineteenth century", "railroad age", "modern age"]
definition: The historical era in which a type of industry was developed, following Stinchcombe's classification into prefactory, early nineteenth century, railroad age, and modern cohorts. The modern age is treated as the base case in the analysis.

name: Census time period
definition: The census year in which an industry's structure is observed, captured by dummy variables for the later census periods with 1950 and 1951 treated as the base years.

name: Canadian control
definition: Industries in Canada whose corporations are controlled by Canadians, contrasted with the same industries in the United States.

name: Foreign control
definition: Industries in Canada that are controlled by foreign firms, most of which are American. In Canada, in sharp contrast to the United States, a large majority of all manufacturing and resource industries are controlled by foreign firms.

name: Enrollment change
definition: Enrollment is average daily attendance computed over the full academic year; changes in enrollments are the difference between enrollments in the 1971-1972 school year and the 1970-1971 school year.

name: Revenue change
definition: The financial variables reflect the amount and source of revenues used by the districts; changes between 1971 and 1972 are measured separately for federal, state and local sources, local revenues being mainly property taxes.

name: Personnel components
authors_terms: ["personnel components", "kinds of personnel", "personnel components and other variables"]
definition: The personnel components were the same as those used by Freeman and Hannan (1975) and were defined in terms of full-time equivalents.

name: Supportive component
definition: The term 'supportive component' refers to all non-teachers, contrasted with the 'direct component' of the teaching staff; SUP = PROF + A + NPS.

name: Direct component
definition: The 'direct component', more general than 'production workers', is the teaching staff: the number of classroom teachers, including substitutes.

name: Administrators
definition: Administrators narrowly defined; certificated employees who do not provide a service directly to pupils (e.g., principals, superintendents, financial officers).

name: Professional staff
definition: The professional staff; certified employees who perform nonteaching services for pupils in direct contact with them (e.g., guidance counselors, librarians, school nurses).

name: Nonprofessional staff
definition: Nonprofessional staff; employees whose jobs do not require educational certification (e.g., janitors, cafeteria workers excluding dieticians, clerks, secretaries).

name: Enrollment growth
definition: A binary variable: growing districts are those that increased, and declining districts those that decreased, in enrollment between 1971 and 1972 and between 1972 and 1973.

name: Tax election experience
authors_terms: ["TAX", "tax elections", "recent experience of the district in tax elections"]
definition: Recent experience of the district in tax elections, measured as a nominal scale scored 'fail', 'pass' or 'no election' and pooled over the years 1970 to 1972.

name: Structural differentiation
definition: The division of labor within an organization, reflected in how evenly employees are distributed among the occupations of the work organization and in the functional distinctiveness among departments.

name: National dominance
definition: The number of agencies or activities in a city that are nationally organized or have national implications, such as scientific research, air transport, corporate headquarters, and cultural opportunity structures.

name: Metropolitan dominance
definition: The extent to which a city dominates its immediate surroundings by acting as a retail trade center, indicated by locally organized activities such as retail trade.

name: Leisure services
definition: The abundance of businesses providing leisure services in a metropolitan community, an increasingly prominent sector of retail economies that generates significant advertising revenue for newspapers.

name: Middle-class population
definition: The proportion of metropolitan residents in the middle class, measured by an aggregate socioeconomic index.

name: Racial heterogeneity
definition: One of the two salient dimensions of heterogeneity in an urban population, referring to the racial composition of a metropolitan population.

name: Occupational heterogeneity
definition: One of the two salient dimensions of heterogeneity in an urban population, referring to the occupational composition of a metropolitan labor force.

name: Competition
definition: The extent to which a metropolitan newspaper market is contested by other newspapers, including the suburban press; measured by how little of total newspaper circulation is accounted for by the two largest newspapers in a metropolitan community.

name: Universalistic decision criteria
authors_terms: ["universalistic criteria", "universalistic criterion", "bureaucratic criteria", "\"fair share\" budgeting", "proportional budgeting"]
definition: Decision criteria for allocating resources that apply uniformly to all subunits, such as uniform proportional ("fair share") budgeting and criteria such as total workload and workload efficiency; the authors note such criteria are potentially consistent with either the bureaucratic or the coalitional model.

name: Political power
definition: Power connotes an ability to influence the actions of another, an ability only evidenced with the successful application of power; unexercised power can only be inferred from variables presumed to condition power. Within a university setting the authors distinguish power inferred from the position of a subunit within the political structure for decision making and power inferred from alliances of subunits with interest groups external to the organization.

name: Discretionary budget increment
definition: That portion of the annual subunit budget increment beyond the increment specified in systemwide decision guidelines, which is controllable by the administration or the subunits; only this measure is utilized to test for the presence of coalitional behavior in budget decision making.

name: Resource availability
authors_terms: ["availability of resources", "relative abundance of resources", "relative scarcity of resources", "periods of relatively abundant and relatively scarce resources"]
definition: The years 1964-1975 are classified into periods of relatively abundant and relatively scarce resources based upon legislative treatment of university requests; scarcity of resources is expected to influence the felt need for joint decision making and the use of power in bargaining.

name: Financial adversity
definition: A period in which external resources decline, so that organizational slack and aspiration levels fall and internal competition increases. The study contrasts years of relative stringency with years of relative plenty in the university's environment.

name: Curriculum responsiveness
authors_terms: ["departmental responsiveness", "curriculum responsiveness", "efforts to increase the attractiveness of the curriculum", "change in the curriculum"]
definition: Change in the curriculum in the direction of making it more attractive to students; the basic question asked of each department was whether its responsiveness was greater between 1971 and 1973 than between 1964 and 1966.

name: Departmental research reputation
definition: The national standing of a department's research, as given by standard reputational rankings. A department able to use a strong research reputation to secure outside funds, student interest, and administrative favor is less dependent on maintaining an attractive curriculum to compete for resources.

name: Internal communication star status
definition: Internal communication stars (the term is borrowed from the early sociometric research) are those individuals most frequently approached as technical discussion partners.

name: Communication with professional areas outside the organization
authors_terms: ["professional domain", "professional areas outside the organization", "professional communication boundary"]
definition: Extra-organizational communication was further separated into a professional domain, that is, communication with universities and professional societies.

name: Communication with operational areas outside the organization
definition: Extra-organizational communication was further separated into an operational domain, that is, communication with suppliers, vendors, and customers.

name: Communication with the larger organization
authors_terms: ["organizational communication", "laboratory to larger organization interface", "communication with areas in the larger organization"]
definition: The boundary between the innovating subsystem and the larger organization; in R&D settings, the communication boundary between the laboratory and the marketing, manufacturing, and sales areas is critical.

name: Communication with other areas of the laboratory
authors_terms: ["intra-laboratory communication", "intralaboratory communication", "communication with other areas, that is, departments, of the laboratory"]
definition: Communication across intra-laboratory interfaces; because innovating subsystems may themselves be highly differentiated, these units face the problem of internal integration.

name: Number of boundary roles
authors_terms: ["special boundary roles", "boundary-spanning roles", "number of boundary roles per project", "boundary roles"]
definition: Individuals filling these roles are capable of translating contrasting coding schemes and therefore of acting as boundary spanners between the work unit and external information areas.

name: Project task complexity
authors_terms: ["project task characteristics", "task characteristics", "task dimension ranging from complex (research) to less complex (technical service)"]
definition: Tasks can differ by length of time required for feedback, specific problem versus general problem orientation, and their generation of new knowledge in contrast to their use of existing knowledge; four task categories were developed with the laboratory's managers to form a task dimension ranging from complex (research) to less complex (technical service).

name: Task environment change
authors_terms: ["project task environment", "stable-changing dimension of the task environment", "changing environment", "stable environment"]
definition: Of the many environmental dimensions studied, Duncan and Negandi and Reimann suggest that the dimension showing the range between stability and change is a particularly important contributor to perceived uncertainty.

name: Project task interdependence
definition: Project-task interdependence refers to the extent to which a task requires working with other areas of the organization.

name: Project performance
definition: An overall technical performance rating of each project; since each project was developing new technologies or new products or revising existing products, this performance measure can be taken as a proxy for the innovativeness of the project.

name: Frequency of interaction
authors_terms: ["frequency of interaction", "frequency of interacting", "frequency of contact"]
definition: The frequency of interactions between community organizations and district offices of the employment service; the dependent variable is the average of the responses of the community organization and the employment service in each relationship.

name: Perceived benefits from interaction
authors_terms: ["benefits from interaction", "perceiving benefits", "perception of benefits", "mutual benefits"]
definition: The extent to which members of an organization perceive that they benefit from interacting with the other organization; the perception of benefits resulting from a relationship is argued to be a good predictor of the frequency of interaction between two organizations.

name: Benefit asymmetry
definition: A situation in which one organization perceives benefits from interacting and the other does not, in contrast to a symmetrical situation in which both organizations perceive benefits or neither does.

name: Goal compatibility
definition: The extent to which the members of an organization perceive the other organization's goals to be compatible with its own; in the asymmetrical situation compatible goals mean those perceiving few benefits perceive little threat in the relationship.

name: Influence of the other organization
authors_terms: ["influence of the other organization", "influence of the employment service", "amount of influence"]
definition: The amount of influence the other organization has on the decisions reached when representatives of the two organizations meet to discuss issues of mutual concern.

name: Importance of the other organization
definition: How important the other organization is for the functioning and operations of the organization; the more important the other organization is to those perceiving few benefits, the more frequent the interaction.

name: Aggressive influence tactics
authors_terms: ["bargaining and conflict-oriented tactics of influence", "aggressive pressure tactics", "bargaining", "conflict"]
definition: Acting aggressively in pursuing one's interests by using bargaining and conflict-oriented tactics of influence; in an asymmetrical relationship these are the pressure-oriented tactics by which the benefiting organization tries to force or induce the other to interact.

name: Formalization of agreements
authors_terms: ["formalization of agreements", "degree to which agreements are formalized", "extent of formalized agreements"]
definition: The degree to which agreements between the two organizations are formalized; formalization is associated with both conflict and cooperation and does not discriminate between the two dimensions.

name: Reciprocity in setting terms
authors_terms: ["reciprocity in setting the terms of interaction", "setting terms of interaction", "amount of reciprocity"]
definition: The amount of reciprocity in setting the terms of interaction between the district office and the community organization.

name: Tension in the relationship
definition: The extent to which tension exists between the two organizations, one of the dimensions of the relationship measured in the study.

name: Organicness of structure
definition: Structure is conceptualized on a mechanistic-organic continuum, and the adjective "organicness" indicates the extent to which an organization possesses what Burns and Stalker would call an organic structure, that is, a structure not characterized by highly specified and delimited job descriptions or highly formalized procedures.

name: Perceived environmental uncertainty
definition: The uncertainty in the environment that is perceived by the organization member; the concept of organizational environment was operationalized as perceived environmental uncertainty because organizational design actions may be more consistent with perceptions of the environment than with objective indicators of environmental conditions.

name: Boundary-spanning activity
definition: In this study, boundary-spanning activity is defined by the total verbal and written interactions with extra work units.

name: Task predictability
definition: Task predictability referred to the extent to which raw materials and task activities associated with the performance of a particular job were well understood and nonproblematic for individuals in that position.

name: Workflow predictability
authors_terms: ["work flow predictability", "workflow predictability", "predictability of the workflow"]
definition: Work flow predictability referred to the extent to which raw materials and transformation processes associated with the combination of tasks carried on by an organizational subunit were well understood and nonproblematic for individuals in the unit.

name: Staff qualifications
definition: Our measures of staff qualifications focused on the nursing staff as the largest and most significant component of the ward staff. One assessed initial level of training and the other measured the extent to which this training was being supplemented and maintained by current professional activities.

name: Staff differentiation
definition: An index of staff differentiation was developed from data obtained from an organization chart constructed during the interview with each head nurse; the larger the number of positions and the more even the distribution of persons among them, the higher the score of a ward on this index.

name: Centralization of decision making
definition: To compute a measure of centralization of decision making for each ward, a two-step procedure was used. First, influence scores for the position of staff nurses and the position of head nurses were calculated; then, the centralization of influence was determined by subtracting the score of the staff nurses in each ward from the score of their head nurse.

name: Standardization of policies and procedures
authors_terms: ["standardization", "standardization of policies and procedures", "standardization of ward procedures and policies"]
definition: By focusing on the extent to which participants perceive that rules have been explicitly formulated to govern specified areas of conduct, we hoped to assess more accurately the degree to which rules, whether written or unwritten, guided behavior.

name: Subunit size
authors_terms: ["subunit size", "ward size", "size of the organizational subunit"]
definition: Our measure of subunit size was the total number of fulltime equivalent staff members employed on each ward.

name: Pattern of joint venture activity
authors_terms: ["pattern of interorganizational linkage activity", "proportion of the industry i's total joint venture activity that was with industry j", "vij"]
definition: The dependent variable is the pattern of interorganizational linkage activity accomplished through joint ventures; for a given industry it is the proportion of that industry's total joint venture activity that was with a given other industry.

name: Purchase interdependence
authors_terms: ["purchase interdependence", "proportion of industry i's purchases from industry j", "pij"]
definition: Purchase interdependence is the proportion of industry i's purchases within the set of 21 industries made from industry j.

name: Sales interdependence
authors_terms: ["sales interdependence", "proportion of industry i's sales to industry j", "sij"]
definition: Sales interdependence is the proportion of industry i's sales made to industry j.

name: Total transactions interdependence
authors_terms: ["total transactions interdependence", "proportion of industry i's total transactions with industry j", "tij"]
definition: Total transactions interdependence is the proportion of industry i's total transactions made with industry j, including both sales and purchases.

name: Industry concentration
authors_terms: ["concentration ratio", "concentration of the organization's economic environment", "industrial concentration"]
definition: The concept of concentration means that the given organization has few competitors for sales, and it presumably gives the organization market power.

name: Technological intensity
authors_terms: ["technological intensity", "proportion of total employment engaged in research and development", "proportion of scientists and engineers in research and development to total industry employment"]
definition: Industries with a high component of research and development costs; measured as the proportion of scientists and engineers in research and development to total industry employment in 1969.

name: Capital intensity
authors_terms: ["capital intensity", "labor intensive industry", "capital output ratio", "labor output ratio"]
definition: The extent to which an industry uses a great deal of capital equipment per unit of output produced, as opposed to labor; high fixed costs are faced in industries that are not labor intensive.

name: Pattern of joint subsidiary location relative to parent industry
authors_terms: ["proportion of industry i's joint subsidiaries that were in industry j"]
definition: The proportion of industry i's joint subsidiaries that were in industry j, formed from a matrix of industry of parent by industry of joint subsidiary.

name: Organizational size
definition: The measure of organizational size is the number of members in the local administrative bureaucracy.

name: Structural complexity
definition: Structural complexity—horizontal differentiation, vertical differentiation, and role specialization.

name: Horizontal differentiation
definition: Horizontal differentiation or width was measured by the number of departments in the organization, a department being any unit having at least two persons and two levels, the head of which reported to the mayor, administrator or an alderman.

name: Vertical differentiation
definition: Vertical differentiation or height was measured by counting the number of levels in each department from the department head to the lowest level worker and then calculating the average for all departments.

name: Role specialization
definition: The measure of role specialization developed by Pugh, Hickson, and their associates (1969) reflected the number of specialized roles across 16 functional areas.

name: Span of control
authors_terms: ["span of control", "average span of control of middle echelon"]
definition: To measure the span of control, the number of subordinates who reported directly to each department head was determined, and then for each organization the mean for all departments was taken, yielding an average span of control for department heads for each organization.

name: Work process formalization
authors_terms: ["work processes", "formality of work process", "work process rigidity", "rigid work processes", "routinization", "autonomy", "rule observance"]
definition: Work processes may be broadly defined as the behavioral patterns involved in the actual conduct of the work; the dimensions examined include the degree of routinization, the degree of autonomy at work, and the degree of rule compliance. The fourth hypothesis asserts that the less formal the work process, the greater the influence.

name: Volume of communication
definition: Interaction processes refer to the processes of information exchange and coordination; that is, communication processes including peer communication, communication with supervisors, and communication with subordinates. Respondents were asked to report the number of contacts, either in face-to-face meetings or by telephone, with persons at the same level, at a lower level, and at a higher level in the organization in a typical week.

name: Influence on decision making
authors_terms: ["influence", "influence on decision making", "influence on strategic decisions", "influence on work decisions"]
definition: The dependent variable in this study was the reported influence of organizational actors, not their authority. Authority is formally constituted power while influence is power which is based both on formal and extra-formal sources; the two measures of influence are influence on strategic decisions and influence on work decisions.

name: Objective isolation
definition: Alienation is defined as an objective state of isolation from others: one person is alienated from another if the surrounding circumstances (including work, or location in some other structure of social relationships) prevent him from engaging in certain types of relationships with the other person. When individuals in an organization are isolated sociometrically from certain categories of members, they are considered objectively alienated from that dimension of organizational activity.

name: Isolation from formal authority
authors_terms: ["isolation from formal authority", "isolation from the formal structure of authority", "isolation from official authority", "isolation from formal control", "isolation from persons in positions of official authority"]
definition: Isolation from persons in positions of official authority, one of four dimensions of objective alienation; the less working contact reported with persons in official authority positions, the more pronounced the isolation on this dimension.

name: Isolation from actual control
authors_terms: ["isolation from the network of perceived actual control", "isolation from actual control", "isolation from informal control"]
definition: Isolation from those seen by respondents as influential in the actual structure of decision making in the organization.

name: Isolation from friends
authors_terms: ["isolation from friends", "isolation from friends in the organization", "isolation from close friends at work"]
definition: Isolation from friends in the organization, assessed by the overlap between the individuals named as close friends and those named as work contacts.

name: Isolation from respected coworkers
authors_terms: ["isolation from highly respected coworkers", "isolation from coworkers whose judgment is most respected", "isolation from respected coworkers", "isolation from respected colleagues"]
definition: Isolation from coworkers whose professional judgment is most respected, assessed by the overlap between those named as most respected and those named as work contacts.

name: Official authority
definition: Official authority based on official title, position and duties, specifically exercising supervisory authority over the work of others; it is one indicator of formal status in the organization.

name: Professional standing
definition: Professional standing measured by a combination of occupation, training and job duties in the organization, with four categories corresponding basically to clerical, service, technical, and professional.

name: Expertise
definition: Expertise in the skills important to the work of the organization, measured by number of years of formal education and by specialized professional training over and above ordinary formal education.

name: Sex
definition: Sex of the member, included because of the different roles typically assigned to men and women in organizations, and measured ordinally with male high to reflect differences in freedom and privileges.

name: Organizational professionalization
definition: The extent to which an organization approximates the abstract professional model, as distinguished by its goals, basic activities, the flexibility of role definitions and the rigidity of its control structures, ranging from commercial through semiprofessional to professional organizations.

name: Level of success of a change project
definition: The level of success of a change project, assessed with a well-defined, behaviorally based scale that provided a measure and/or a description of sample behavior for each rating point.

name: Favorable forces in unfreezing
definition: Forces that favor unfreezing, the phase of behavior that increases the receptivity of the client system to a possible change in the distribution and balance of social forces.

name: Unfavorable forces in unfreezing
definition: Forces unfavorable to unfreezing, i.e., resistance to the phase of behavior that increases the receptivity of the client system to a possible change in the distribution and balance of social forces.

name: Favorable forces in moving
definition: Forces that favor moving, the phase of altering the magnitude, direction, or number of driving and resisting forces, consequently shifting the equilibrium to a new level.

name: Unfavorable forces in moving
definition: Forces unfavorable to moving, i.e., resistance to the phase of altering the magnitude, direction, or number of driving and resisting forces and shifting the equilibrium to a new level.

name: Favorable forces in refreezing
definition: Forces that favor refreezing, the phase of reinforcing the new distribution of forces, thereby maintaining and stabilizing the new social equilibrium.

name: Unfavorable forces in refreezing
definition: Forces unfavorable to refreezing, i.e., resistance to the phase of reinforcing the new distribution of forces and stabilizing the new social equilibrium.

name: Behavior control
authors_terms: ["behavior control", "control based on direct, personal surveillance", "personal surveillance", "personal control"]
definition: Control based on direct, personal surveillance.

name: Output control
authors_terms: ["output control", "control based on the measurement of outputs", "management by files or records", "impersonal control"]
definition: Control based on the measurement of outputs.

name: Knowledge of means-ends relations
authors_terms: ["understanding of means-ends relationships", "knowledge of means-ends relations", "technical knowledge", "supervisor's expertise"]
definition: The extent to which a manager understands the relation between behavior and outcomes, measured by how much a manager can tell by watching the people who report to him while they work and by how familiar a supervisor is with the respondent's on-the-job performance. The authors note that if means-end relations were not understood, behavior control was not functional, since the appropriate behavior was not known.

name: Need to provide legitimate evidence of performance
authors_terms: ["need to provide legitimate evidence of performance", "need to defend his position", "tactic of self-legitimation"]
definition: A manager's need to provide legitimate evidence of his performance, which the authors argue governs the use of output control.

name: Task interdependence
definition: The extent to which a person's performance depends upon how well others do their job.

name: Routine work
definition: The percentage of time on the job spent carrying out routine tasks.

name: Task complexity
definition: How long it would take an inexperienced person to learn the basics necessary to handling the job.

name: Hierarchical level
definition: The respondent's level in the hierarchy, assigned by comparing job title with organization charts; levels 1-5 were within the stores, levels 6 and 7 within the corporations that owned the stores and were excluded from the study.

name: Company membership
authors_terms: ["company", "membership in either Company A ... or Company B"]
definition: Membership in one of the two companies that owned the stores; Company A had approximately 2,000 employees and Company B approximately 8,000 employees.

name: Organizational orientation
definition: Orientation is defined by the proportion of total income derived from production activities: organizations with half or more of their income from production activities were classified as production-oriented; those with less than half of their income from this source were classified as rehabilitation-oriented. Where a relatively high proportion of total income came from production activities, clients were viewed as employees and thus as instruments of production, and where a relatively low proportion came from production activities, clients were viewed as individuals needing therapy.

name: Period of organizational founding
authors_terms: ["date of organizational founding", "date of founding", "period of organizational foundation"]
definition: Organizations were classified by whether they were founded before and during World War II or founded after World War II; the dividing line for the earlier and later period of workshops was 1946.

name: Income from grants
definition: Income received by the workshop in the form of grants, as distinct from income from production activities; workshops were distinguished by whether they had no income from grants or some income from grants.

name: Goal incompatibility
definition: Goals are operationally defined as the criteria used by city decision-making units to order their preferences on decisions relating to collective bargaining. Goal incompatibility is assumed to be institutionalized in the city-management structure, especially among city officials who are interdependent in collective bargaining.

name: Ability to interfere with goal attainment
authors_terms: ["ability to interfere with the goal attainment of others", "ability of a unit to interfere with the goal attainment of another unit", "interference capability"]
definition: Within an interdependent relationship various situational characteristics will create differences in the ability of one party to engage in conflict with another. Since overt conflict will be affected by the abilities of some units to interfere with the goal attainment of the others, the greater this ability, the more internal conflict there will be.

name: Dispersion of power
definition: The extent to which power is shared among a number of city officials rather than concentrated in a hierarchical ordering; Cormick (1971) explicitly stated that shared power is the dynamic that explains whether potential conflict turns into actual conflict.

name: Dispersion of control
authors_terms: ["dispersion of control", "shared control", "control over bargaining decisions is shared"]
definition: The extent to which control over bargaining decisions is shared among decision makers in city management; the concept of control, as Tannenbaum defined it, is closely related to the authors' concept of the dispersion of power.

name: Jurisdictional ambiguity
authors_terms: ["jurisdictional ambiguity", "ambiguity over who has authority to make bargaining decisions"]
definition: Ambiguity or uncertainty over the authority relationships among organizational subunits; in the literature on bargaining in the public sector it is cast in terms of the question of who is management in the public sector.

name: Pressure in negotiations
authors_terms: ["pressure in negotiations", "pressure within negotiations", "perceived negotiations pressure"]
definition: The pressure that management officials feel is being applied by the employee organization in negotiations, through threats to engage in job actions or threats to use the state dispute-resolution procedures.

name: Internal conflict
definition: Overt conflict behavior among interdependent city decision-making units engaged in collective bargaining, which conflict theorists distinguish from the mere existence of conflicts of interests, values, or goals.

name: Organization development interventions
definition: Organization development (OD), a philosophy of and technology for producing organizational change, is a pastiche of techniques developed in the behavioral sciences which focus on problems of organizational learning, motivation, problem solving, communications, and interpersonal relations. In this plant the effort was a six-phase program concentrated on the production group.

name: Perceptions of organizational climate
authors_terms: ["organizational climate", "perceptions of organizational climate", "team effectiveness questionnaire"]
definition: Perceptions of organizationally anchored phenomena measured with a questionnaire developed by Douglas McGregor for use in team building, which asked respondents to rate such factors as trust, support, communication, understanding of objectives, commitment to objectives, handling of conflict, utilization of resources, control methods, and organizational environment.

name: Perceptions of supervisory behavior
definition: Perceptions of the behavior of the immediate supervisor measured with a questionnaire developed by Ed Nevis for use in OD projects and modified for this study, asking employees to describe their supervisors relative to listening, expressing ideas to others, influence style, decision making, relations with others, task orientation, handling of conflict, willingness to change, problem solving, and self development.

name: Production rate
definition: An index of organizational performance, the number of units produced per month, recorded on a daily basis and averaged across the periods.

name: Variance in production rate
authors_terms: ["variance in the production index", "variance in production levels", "variance in units produced"]
definition: The amount of variance around the average level of production, a separate dimension of performance hypothesized to change because improved planning, decision making, problem solving, and use of internal resources would increase the predictability of the flow of outputs from period to period.

name: Quality level
authors_terms: ["quality index", "quality levels", "quality units", "number of quality units"]
definition: An index of organizational performance: the average number of units produced per month which did not require repair or rework.

name: Variance in quality index
authors_terms: ["variance in the quality index", "variance in quality levels"]
definition: The variance around the level of the quality index, a dimension of performance predicted to decrease as a result of the OD change effort.

name: Profit
authors_terms: ["profit index", "profit or loss", "performance to budget", "profit level"]
definition: An index of organizational performance, monthly profit or loss (performance to budget), averaged across the periods.

name: Mass output orientation of operations technology
authors_terms: ["mass-output orientation of operations technology", "mass production orientation of technology", "mass-output orientation of technology", "mass production orientation of the firm's operations"]
definition: Technology refers here to the manufacturing, as distinct from administrative or distributive, processes employed by manufacturing firms to convert inputs into outputs. The measure yields an index of how mass-output oriented was each firm's technology, so that firms using primarily custom and/or small-batch technologies score substantially less than firms primarily using mass-production and/or continuous-process technologies.

name: Vertical integration
authors_terms: ["vertical integration", "extent of vertical integration of firm"]
definition: Generally, vertical integration in manufacturing firms means acquiring or getting control over factors of production—raw materials, parts, fuels, ideas—and channels of distribution—wholesaling, retailing, and so forth.

name: Decentralization of top-level decision making
authors_terms: ["decentralization of top-level decisions", "delegation of authority", "decentralization of decision-making authority by the chief executive"]
definition: While there are many different measures of decentralization, the one adopted for this study emphasized the decentralization of top-management decision making. The president rated the extent to which the chief executive officer of the firm had delegated decision-making authority in each of nine key areas of decision making.

name: Use of sophisticated controls
authors_terms: ["use of sophisticated controls", "usage of sophisticated controls", "sophisticated control and information system"]
definition: Most organizations of any size develop a host of controls and procedures to regulate work processes and the behavior of organizational members. The use of sophisticated controls is, however, likely to vary significantly between organizations because they are expensive to operate and require substantial information processing skills on the part of managers who utilize them.

name: Firm size
definition: The size of the firm was measured by taking the natural logarithm of its annual sales.

name: Long-term profitability
authors_terms: ["long-term profitability", "average profitability of firm", "rate of return on net worth"]
definition: The firm's long-term profitability was measured by averaging the highest rate of profit on net worth with the lowest such rate during the previous five years.

name: Subunit power
definition: Power was the ability of the department to affect decisions so that they conformed more closely to what the department wanted; power is defined as potential influence.

name: Resource contribution to the organization
authors_terms: ["provide resources for the organization", "provision of resources", "the extent to which the subunit provides resources to the organization", "subunit's relative contribution of resources"]
definition: The extent to which the subunit actually contributes resources, including knowledge, to the organization. It was hypothesized in this study that subunits will possess relatively more power to the extent they provide resources for the organization.

name: Resource scarcity
definition: Scarcity implies that there is not enough of the resource for every department to get all it would like and is defined by the amount of the resource available divided by the amount requested.

name: Resource criticality
definition: Criticality was defined as the extent to which the resource is absolutely necessary for the effective operation of the department.

name: Subunit attempts to acquire resources
authors_terms: ["make attempts to acquire it", "vie for a resource"]
definition: The extent to which a subunit will make attempts to acquire a resource, which the authors argue depends on the criticality of the resource to the subunit's effective operation.

name: Objective allocation criteria
authors_terms: ["objective criteria", "objective bases of resource allocation", "universalistic bureaucratic criteria"]
definition: Indicators of objective criteria for allocating the four resources, obtained from discussions with persons involved in the allocation decisions and representing quantity indicators of a department's need for a resource independent of its assessment of the criticality of the resource.

name: Use of power in resource allocation
authors_terms: ["use of power", "power is used to allocate it", "power as the basis of its allocation"]
definition: The use of power in the allocation of resources within the organization; it is hypothesized that power is used in the allocation of an organizational resource to the extent that the resource is scarce within the organization.

name: Organizational resource criticality
definition: The extent to which resources provided by a subunit are critical, important, or valued by the organization.

name: State political culture
authors_terms: ["state political culture", "political culture", "type of political culture"]
definition: According to Elazar, each of the 48 mainland states may be characterized as having one of three pure political culture types: traditionalistic, moralistic, or individualistic. The meaningful context of the state planning and development agency is the state within which the agency is located, and it is particularly the political aspect of the cultural context that is of importance.

name: State government innovation
definition: According to Walker, "an innovation is simply a program or policy that is new to the state adopting it."

name: Fiscal support for change-agent organizations
authors_terms: ["financial support provided change-agent organizations", "fiscal support", "state support"]
definition: The amount of funds available for agency operations, expressed as the ratio of the planning and development organization budget to total state expenditures, taken as a measure of the extent of support given to change-agent organizations.

name: Abstractness of change-agent activities
authors_terms: ["abstract activities", "character of organizational activity", "less immediate product or outcome"]
definition: An abstract activity was defined as one having means-ends relationships that were not readily apparent or that did not lead to an immediate result.

name: Presence of a specialized buffering structure
authors_terms: ["specialized structure associated with the organization to protect it from its environment", "board or commission", "parent board or commission"]
definition: A specialized structure, an agency board or commission, whose most important purpose is to act as a buffer and shield the organization from external disturbances and threats.

name: Change-agent organization type
definition: Agency directors identified their organization as a planning organization, one which gave primary emphasis to planning, or as a development organization, one which gave primary emphasis to development; where the director indicated that equal emphasis was given to planning and development, the agency was termed a miscellaneous organization.

name: Management by objectives program
definition: Conceptually MBO is thought of as an approach that will influence the total management hierarchy of an organization, which is assumed by advocates eventually to reach first-line supervisors, who will then become more effective members of the management team; this increased effectiveness should be reflected in improved performance among the subordinates of these trained, and involved supervisors.

name: Positive reinforcement
authors_terms: ["variable ratio reinforcement schedule", "variable reinforcement schedule", "positive reinforcement", "reinforcement program", "reinforcement schedule"]
definition: A variable schedule, in which the time varies between reinforcements, chosen for plant E2 and designed to demonstrate that top management continued to support MBO actively, to show that the training program was important, and to inform participants that help or counseling was available.

name: Employee performance
definition: The performance of the operating employees who were the subordinates of the first-line supervisors: line workers in the production unit and salesmen in the marketing unit, whose performance was studied to determine the influence of MBO at this vital level of the organization. Only objective performance measures were used.

name: Scale and diversification of municipal government
authors_terms: ["scale and diversification of municipal government", "municipal index", "scale and diversification of municipal government"]
definition: The study's first organizational source of integration: the scale of a city's government, measured by municipal employment, and the diversification signified by the number of municipal agencies and the spread of municipal expenditures across service categories, subject to formal imperative coordination with one another.

name: Community-wide voluntary associations
definition: The extent to which voluntary associations are uncontested and community-wide; such associations pursue diffuse goals, may not take sides in controversy, and constitute a means of dampening strong interorganizational contest through overlapping memberships of organizational elites.

name: Need for interorganizational relations
definition: The need for interorganizational relations arises from awareness of interdependence with other organizations, from the sheer number of organizations of a given type such as hospitals that generates mutual need to regulate competition and institutionalize conflict, and can also result in outside pressures to establish formal interorganizational relations.

name: Formal relations among hospitals
definition: Formal relations among hospitals, of which the hospital council is viewed as the means of meeting the hospitals' needs to establish formal relations with one another as well as meeting other organizations' needs to have the hospitals do this.

name: Complexity of antipoverty networks
authors_terms: ["complex antipoverty networks", "complexity of antipoverty networks", "complex Neighborhood Youth Corps networks"]
definition: Interorganizational complexity of antipoverty networks, scored by whether a city had Neighborhood Youth Corps projects that were part of a complex interorganizational network, formed as part of the war on poverty.

name: Hospital ownership
definition: The type of sponsor controlling the general hospital, distinguishing governmentally controlled city and county and Veterans Administration hospitals from profit-making and nonprofit private general hospitals; environmental constraints on organizations differ as a function of ownership or sponsorship.

name: Department size
definition: Size of department was measured by the number of beds devoted solely to inpatient psychiatric care.

name: Department performance
definition: The relative efficiency of the psychiatric department in utilizing resources and performing its boundary-spanning function, assessed by discharge rate and by the cost of care; discharge rate is recognized as not necessarily a measure of department effectiveness or quality of care.

name: Relative size of administrative staff
authors_terms: ["relative size of the administrative staff", "administrative staff", "size of administrative staff"]
definition: The relative size of the administrative staff in the department, measured as administrative staff man-hours per unit of department size.

name: Relative size of professional staff
authors_terms: ["relative size of the professional staff", "professionalization of staff", "professional or semi-professional staff"]
definition: The relative size of the professional or technical staff in the department, measured as professional staff man-hours per unit of department size.

name: Input and output buffers
definition: Structures that smooth environmental influences by surrounding the core treatment technology, on the input side by identifying and restricting homogeneous elements of the task environment, and on the output side by facilitating the flow of patients out of the inpatient department.

name: Number of directors
authors_terms: ["number of directors", "size of the board of directors", "board size"]
definition: The number of members serving on the organization's board of directors, treated as a dependent variable reflecting the organization's need to coopt external elements of its environment.

name: Percentage of inside directors
authors_terms: ["percentage of inside directors", "percentage of outsiders", "inside-outside orientation"]
definition: Inside directors are defined as directors that are either current managers in the organization or retired or former managers for the same organization, with subsidiary organizations assumed to be within the organization under consideration.

name: Representation of financial institutions on the board
authors_terms: ["percentage of board members representing financial institutions", "representatives of financial institutions"]
definition: The percentage of the board of directors composed of representatives from financial institutions with which the organization is interdependent.

name: Percentage of attorneys on the board
authors_terms: ["percentage of attorneys", "percentage of attorneys on boards of directors"]
definition: The share of the board of directors made up of attorneys, who are expected to appear more often as boards become more externally oriented and as the use of outside financing increases the need for legal services and advice.

name: Need for access to external capital markets
authors_terms: ["need for access to external capital markets", "requirements for external financing", "need for access to the capital markets"]
definition: The organization's requirements for external financing and ready access to the capital markets, which create interdependence with organizations that provide funds.

name: Organizational regulation
authors_terms: ["regulated industries", "nationally regulated", "locally regulated", "whether or not the organization is regulated"]
definition: Whether the organization operates under regulation, with the paper distinguishing local regulation, which must tap essentially local political power bases, from national regulation, which emanates from Washington and is more legalistic and formal.

name: Organizational size
authors_terms: ["size of the organization", "total sales volume", "size of the firm"]
definition: The size of the organization, which increases its need for a larger board because large organizations are typically more diversified and have a greater impact on society and the economy.

name: Deviation from preferred inside-outside board composition
authors_terms: ["deviations from optimal board structure", "DIF", "deviation from a preferred board composition"]
definition: The absolute value of the difference between the actual percentage of insiders and the percentage predicted for the organization by the estimated board-composition equation.

name: Performance relative to industry standards
authors_terms: ["company performance", "financial effectiveness", "success compared to industry standards"]
definition: Organizational profitability measured relative to standards for the organization's industry, using the ratio of net income to sales and the ratio of net income to stockholders' equity.

name: Environmental complexity
definition: The simple part of the simple-complex dimension deals with the degree to which the factors in the decision unit's environment are few in number and are similar to one another in that they are located in a few components. The complex phase indicates that the factors in the decision unit's environment are large in number.

name: Environmental dynamism
definition: The static-dynamic dimension is viewed as the degree to which these factors in the decision unit's environment remain basically the same over time or are in a continual process of change. The static-dynamic dimension indicates the degree to which the factors of the decision unit's internal and external environment remain basically the same over time or are in a continual process of change.

name: Perceived environmental uncertainty
definition: The present definition of uncertainty thus takes a broader perspective and is concerned with the individual's ability to assign probabilities. Three components of uncertainty were mentioned: the lack of information regarding the environmental factors associated with a given decision-making situation, not knowing the outcome of a specific decision in terms of how much the organization would lose if the decision were incorrect, and inability to assign probabilities with any degree of confidence with regard to how environmental factors are going to affect the success or failure of the decision unit.

name: Change agent origin
authors_terms: ["internal change agent", "external change agent", "internal versus external change agent", "role of the associate dean"]
definition: The key variable in the experiment was the role of the associate dean; the object was to compare the differences in budget content and processes resulting from changes introduced by someone who has member status in the group and someone external to the group.

name: Perceived conflict
authors_terms: ["perceived conflict", "level of conflict", "conflict in the group"]
definition: The attempt by an associate dean who is new to the group to introduce a new budgetary method should arouse feelings of hostility and resentment in group members; these feelings should be expressed through conflict over interpersonal issues and lead to substantive conflict over budgetary issues.

name: Tension between dean and associate dean
authors_terms: ["perceived level of tension between the dean and the associate dean", "tension between the dean and the associate dean"]
definition: The tension created between the dean and the associate dean when the associate dean's role of instructor challenges the dean's established leadership position.

name: Threat to group harmony
authors_terms: ["threat to the harmony of the group", "perceived threat to harmony"]
definition: The necessity for adjusting interpersonal relationships during the introduction of change would pose a threat to the group's harmony.

name: Threat to authority structure
authors_terms: ["threat to the group's authority structure", "perceived threat to authority"]
definition: The external associate dean's higher level of perceived expertise would give him the basis for exercising authority and influence in his group, thus posing a greater threat to the group's authority structure.

name: Threat to effectiveness
authors_terms: ["threat to the effectiveness of the group", "perceived threat to the level of the group's effectiveness"]
definition: The combination of threats to the authority structure and harmony of the groups was expected to result in a greater perceived threat to the effectiveness of their groups.

name: Acceptance of the budgeting method
authors_terms: ["acceptance of the budgeting method", "perceived helpfulness of budgetary approach used", "having the method they introduce accepted"]
definition: The readiness with which group members accept the budgetary method introduced by their associate dean; perceived helpfulness of the budgetary approach used is employed as a rough indication of a method's acceptance by members of the group.

name: Conformity to the budgeting method
authors_terms: ["conformity to the budgeting method", "followed the method introduced by their associate deans"]
definition: How closely the group followed the budgetary method introduced by its associate dean.

name: Change agent influence
authors_terms: ["level of influence of internal associate deans", "influence of external associate deans"]
definition: The level of influence exercised in the group by the associate dean relative to the dean, as indicated by group members' rankings.

name: Routineness of work
authors_terms: ["degree of routineness of work", "routineness of technology", "routine work-flow", "routine work"]
definition: If the clients are stable and uniform and much is known about the particular process of treatment, then the organization has a routine work-flow; the degree of routineness is one dimension of technology that can be applied equally to people-processing, industrial, and other kinds of organizations.

name: Centralization of organizational power
authors_terms: ["centralization of organizational power", "centralization of decision-making", "degree of participation in organizational decisions"]
definition: The concentration of power over basic organizational decisions; if organizational members constantly face a work situation characterized by highly varied client needs, greater organizational power accrues to members who interact with clients most frequently and decision-making is decentralized.

name: Formalization of organizational roles
definition: The formalization of organizational roles, reflected in various types of rules and regulations defining role obligations and enactment, such as policy manuals, job descriptions or evaluation procedures.

name: Professional training of staff
authors_terms: ["amount of professional training", "professional training", "less well trained staff"]
definition: The amount of professional training of the staff, treated by the authors as one of the measures of the degree of complexity of the organization; a straight-forward client interview creates little need for job occupants with advanced degrees, whereas using psychiatric skills requires at a minimum a master's degree.

name: Organizational complexity
definition: The degree of complexity of the organization, measured by the amount of professional training, the amount of professional activity, and the number of occupational specialties.

name: Organizational stratification
definition: The stratification of the organization, measured by the degree of affect between supervisors and staff and the degree of social distance between supervisors and staff.
