Two individuals may take different stances on a focal issue but still vary in the extent to which their schemas of concepts closely related to the issue align.

name: Observability of latent cognition
authors_terms: ["observability of latent cognition", "observable latent cognition", "obscured latent cognition", "observable versus obscured latent cognition"]
definition: Although the semantic associations that exist in others' minds are not directly accessible, they can be inferred to varying degrees through indirect means, for example based on past actions or displayed symbols; when people become aware of how an opposing other's latent cognition differs from or resembles their own, a similarity-attraction response is theorized to be activated. When latent cognitive differences are obscured, no information about the source's schemas is provided.

name: Social influence
authors_terms: ["social influence", "changing one's mind", "opinion change", "willingness to change their mind"]
definition: Social influence is the likelihood of changing one's mind about an issue after being exposed to the arguments of another individual who has a different stance.

name: Common ownership
definition: Common ownership is the extent to which a firm's largest and most powerful shareholders are also beneficial owners of other firms. Empirically, it is the equal- or value-weighted average of the profit weights κij that the owners of firm i place in year t on the profits of the n−1 other firms in the economy.

name: Corporate innovation
definition: Corporate innovation is firms' innovative activity. In the model, innovation xi lowers marginal cost; empirically it is measured by innovation inputs (scaled R&D expenditures) and innovation outputs (citation-weighted patents and the total stock market value of patents).

name: Technological proximity
definition: Technological proximity proxies for the potential for technological spillovers between firms: firm i's innovation may lower the marginal costs of technologically related firms j, captured by βij. It is measured by the overlap in patents between each pair of firms in particular technology classes (TECHij).

name: Product market proximity
authors_terms: ["product market spillovers", "product market proximity", "product market competition", "HPij", "a ij"]
definition: Product market proximity, or product market spillovers, is the degree of substitutability/product homogeneity between firms' products, captured by aij. It proxies for business stealing: the more similar the products, the more innovation steals market share from rivals. It is measured by the product cosine similarity of 10-K product descriptions (HPij).

name: Network closure in acquirer role relationships
authors_terms: ["network closure in his or her acquirer role", "density of ties in his or her information acquirer role relationships", "acquirer network density", "ego network density in the acquirer role"]
definition: The extent to which a knowledge worker's contacts in the relationships in which he or she acts as an acquirer of information have ties with one another, measured by the density of ties among alters in the acquirer relationship set.

name: Network closure in provider role relationships
authors_terms: ["network closure in his or her provider role", "density of ties in his or her information provider role relationships", "provider network density", "ego network density in the information provider role"]
definition: The extent to which a knowledge worker's contacts in the relationships in which he or she acts as a provider of information have ties with one another, measured by the density of ties among alters in the provider relationship set.

name: Knowledge worker performance
definition: The annual bonus received by the banker for performance in the 2001 calendar year; bonuses are the main means through which investment banks reward performance.

name: Formal rank
definition: The actor's rank in the hierarchy of the organization, captured by the corporate title of the employee in 2001; rank affects the volume and complexity of the deals a banker participates in and is a lever for control.

name: Crowding from below
authors_terms: ["crowding from below", "encroachment", "crowding by lower-ranked competitors", "crowding by inferiors", "crowding just below an actor"]
definition: CB it captures the number of lower-ranked drivers capable of passing driver i in the points distribution in race t.

name: Crowding from above
authors_terms: ["crowding from above", "opportunity", "crowding by superiors", "crowding by higher-ranked competitors"]
definition: This measure captures the count of higher-ranked drivers whom i could surpass if i received the maximum number of points, and they finished last, in other words, the opportunity of driver i to surpass rivals ranked higher in the points distribution.

name: Risk taking
authors_terms: ["risk taking", "risky conduct", "risky behavior", "tendency to take risks", "risk-taking"]
definition: Our assumption is that a crash is more likely if a driver attempts risky maneuvers on the track. Thus the rate of crashing, which is observable, is treated as a proxy for the unobservable tendency of a competitor to take risks.

name: Rank change
authors_terms: ["rank change", "race-to-race turnover in ranks", "rank stability", "stability of a collection of ranks"]
definition: We collected the ranks of each driver in the Winston Cup series points distribution at the start of the prior race and at the end of the prior race and then identified the number of drivers who underwent a transition in rank.

name: Assessed performance level
authors_terms: ["performance rating", "performance level", "performance category", "assessed performance", "position in the performance distribution"]
definition: An employee's position in the performance distribution, described by the authors in terms of employees classified as extremely high, above-average, below-average, or extremely low performers. Who stays and who leaves organizations should depend on position in the performance distribution.

name: Turnover intention
authors_terms: ["turnover intention", "turnover intentions", "intentions of departure", "intentions of leaving"]
definition: Employees' stated intentions of leaving the firm, used as the dependent outcome instead of actual turnover because intentions of leaving are strongly correlated with subsequent departure and are the single best predictor of turnover.

name: Perceived-assessed performance discrepancy
authors_terms: ["perceived difference score", "difference between perceived and assessed performance", "difference between perceived and rated performance", "discrepancy between perceived and assessed performance"]
definition: The degree to which employees differ in how they perceive their own performance relative to the performance assessed for them; the larger this perceived discrepancy, the more likely is departure.

name: Performance-based pay distinctions
authors_terms: ["performance-based pay distinctions", "performance distinctions", "pay distinctions based on performance", "yearly salary increases"]
definition: Pay differences based on performance, which reflect the limited dispersion in performance ratings and are constrained in large part by the number of performance distinctions an employer makes.

name: Promotion
definition: Promotion through the six job grades through which engineering personnel could be promoted; rewards are also distributed through promotion and promotion's impact on pay.

name: Temporary worker hiring rate
authors_terms: ["temporary hiring rate", "hiring of temporary workers", "rate at which temporaries entered the organization", "hiring temporaries"]
definition: The rate at which temporary workers were hired from outside into the job's mobility cluster; r is the rate at which temporaries entered the organization.

name: Waiting time until promotion
authors_terms: ["waiting time until promotion", "expected waiting time until promotion", "waiting times"]
definition: The expected waiting time until promotion for the organization's permanent workers; the probability of promotion is an inverse function of the expected waiting time until promotion.

name: Promotion type
definition: Promotions that occur through movement into job vacancies that exist apart from and prior to the incumbent versus upgrade promotions, in which a worker receives a higher rank without being placed in a vacant job, possibly because of expanded duties or skills.

name: Permeability of organizational labor markets to outside entry
authors_terms: ["permeability to outside entry", "less permeable", "permeable organization", "openness of job clusters to competition from outside an organization"]
definition: The degree to which an internal labor market is open to competition from the external labor market. An ILM with extremely restricted outside entry can be fully insulated from outside competition if its entry job is filled by a nonpromotable worker.

name: Human resource subunit effectiveness
authors_terms: ["human resource subunit's effectiveness", "subunit effectiveness", "effectiveness assessment", "effectiveness ratings"]
definition: The assessment by a constituency of the focal human resource subunit: as part of its open system, the subunit earns constituency support by producing something of value to its environment and is then viewed or judged favorably by its constituencies; preference satisfaction is the major basis of the effectiveness judgment.

name: Constituency type
authors_terms: ["constituency", "constituent", "stakeholder group", "executive constituency", "manager constituency", "nonmanagement employee constituency", "hierarchically defined constituencies"]
definition: "Constituency" refers to a group of individuals holding similar preferences or interests pertaining to the activities of a focal organizational unit, and the term "constituent" refers to a single individual within a constituency or a stakeholder group.

name: Environmental resource munificence
definition: A munificent environment is characterized by an abundance of resources, financial and other, available to the HR subunit; a low personnel ratio is one indicator of a munificent environment and corporate HR groups may also provide other, intellectual resources such as advice, consultation, and new programs.

name: Demographic heterogeneity of constituents
authors_terms: ["demographic heterogeneity of the constituents", "heterogeneity in constituency demography", "environmental heterogeneity"]
definition: One source of heterogeneity in the task environment of the HR subunit is the demographic composition of its constituents; employees of different age, race, or gender may have different needs that require satisfaction by the HR subunit, and heterogeneity requires a diverse set of responses by the subunit.

name: Co-optation
definition: Co-optation is important for soliciting constituency support and moves the subunit "from stakeholder influence to stakeholder participation"; constituencies may be co-opted by the HR subunit through mechanisms such as advisory boards or HR committees, which involve them in managing the subunit's affairs.

name: Responsiveness
definition: Responsiveness is aimed at addressing constituency needs or concerns in an appropriate and timely fashion.

name: Employee absenteeism
definition: An employee outcome that constituencies may expect the HR subunit to be responsible for, since the subunit is expected to be responsible for employee outcomes such as low absenteeism.

name: Employee grievances
definition: An employee outcome that constituencies may expect the HR subunit to be responsible for, since the subunit is expected to be responsible for the prevention and resolution of grievances.

name: Employee career advancement
authors_terms: ["career advancement", "female and minority promotions", "employee career outcome", "career development of female and minority employees"]
definition: A favorable employee career outcome that constituencies may expect of the HR subunit; only female and minority promotions were measured because the HR subunit usually is expected to play a larger role in the career development of these employees than of white male employees.

name: Adaptive responses
definition: Adaptive responses may include both process and outcome variables: process variables refer to how the HR subunit relates to its constituencies, and outcome variables refer to the results expected of the HR subunit by its various constituencies.

name: Independent contracting
definition: Workers who provide services directly to a client firm on an explicitly short-term basis and without entering into a formal employment relationship with that firm.

name: Family responsibilities
definition: Workers with a need to provide for dependents are more concerned than those without dependents about their ability to moderate their expenditures in response to income fluctuations.

name: Negative cues in work history
definition: Of particular importance is the absence of 'negative cues'-information that casts doubt on whether a worker will make a good long-term employee. Such information might include involuntary separations from previous jobs or long periods of time that are unaccounted for.

name: Skills
definition: To the extent that firms are unwilling to train contractors, they require them to already possess the necessary skills when hired; ethnographies of contractors emphasize that firms expect them to 'hit the ground running.'

name: Work experience
definition: Our measure of experience was the difference between the date that a worker's focal job began and the date that his or her first job began, minus any time that the worker spent out of the labor market.

name: Contracting duration
definition: We combined all contiguous contracting job spells (reducing the total number of spells). We then defined a spell as long-term if it was equal to or over one year in duration.

name: Job security
definition: Historically, internal labor markets gave workers substantial job security through seniority rules for layoffs, formal or informal job guarantees, and entitlements to severance pay, which raise termination costs.

name: Employer-provided training
definition: In internal labor markets, workers and firms gain a joint understanding of the career ladders along which workers should progress, helping workers and firms to anticipate the formal and informal training that will be needed.

name: Stock exchange adoption
authors_terms: ["creation of a stock exchange", "stock market creation", "adoption of a stock exchange"]
definition: The creation of a national stock exchange, treated by the authors as a country-level policy decision emerging from a distributed policy making and implementation process; measured as the time of establishment of a country's first stock exchange.

name: Stock market vibrancy
definition: The vibrancy of the stock markets created between 1980 and 2005, understood by the authors as growth in size in terms of equities listed and market capitalization.

name: Investor-based institutional endowment
authors_terms: ["historical conditions favoring investor-based systems", "national institutional endowment", "prior institutional endowment", "institutional legacy"]
definition: A historically evolved institutional matrix of cultural and political arrangements that enables some but constrains other development directions; the conditions favoring investor-based systems comprise Protestantism, British colonial influence, political democracy, and nonsocialist ideology.

name: Concessional aid dependence
authors_terms: ["dependence on international aid", "financially dependent", "financial dependency on international agencies"]
definition: A country's immediate financial dependency on international agencies and core countries, which provides the structural linkage for coercive power and is expected to increase the influence of the global elite over local policies.

name: Trade competition
definition: Diffusion through competition, in which policy makers are driven by the actions of other states with which they compete in the global economy; the most relevant competitors are those that trade with the same third parties, so competition is cast as structural equivalence in the world trade system.

name: Intercountry learning
definition: Diffusion through drawing on the experiences of others, particularly those seen to be successful pioneers and relevant peers, which relies on proximity and direct channels of communication such as shared regional identity and trade ties.

name: Normative emulation
definition: Adoption of policies because they are normatively appropriate, in which policy makers look to prestigious others and follow the advice of elite professional communities in order to maintain their own status, even in the absence of detailed insight and resources for implementation.

name: Supervisor support
definition: Supportive supervisor behavior toward newcomers, such as taking a personal interest in newcomers' development and forgiving honest mistakes, which newcomers appraise as pleasant and as an aid to goal achievement.

name: Supervisor verbal aggression
definition: Supervisors' verbal aggression, which includes behaviors such as making derogatory remarks, using harsh language, and being rude with newcomers.

name: Newcomer positive affect
definition: A newcomer's conscious, remembered, and accumulated experience of affect in relation to his or her supervisor; newcomer affect can be positive (newcomer positive affect) or negative (newcomer negative affect).

name: Newcomer negative affect
definition: A newcomer's conscious, remembered, and accumulated experience of affect in relation to his or her supervisor; newcomer affect can be positive (newcomer positive affect) or negative (newcomer negative affect).

name: Feedback seeking
definition: Feedback seeking is a deliberate and proactive action by newcomers to search for information about how well they are doing in their new organization. Simply put, feedback seeking refers to an employee voluntarily asking his/her supervisor, 'How am I doing?'

name: Interaction avoidance
authors_terms: ["interaction avoidance", "interaction avoidance vis-a-vis his/her supervisor", "avoidance behavior directed toward a newcomer's supervisor"]
definition: Avoidance behavior directed toward the newcomer's supervisor, such as separating oneself from one's supervisor or trying to escape from a difficult situation; newcomers avoid interacting with the supervisor in the future.

name: Newcomer adjustment
definition: Newcomer adjustment is the extent to which new employees are clear about their role in their organization (role clarity), have developed cordial relationships with colleagues (social adjustment), and have mastered their day-to-day tasks (task mastery).

name: In-role performance
definition: The extent to which a newcomer satisfactorily completes the responsibilities associated with his or her role.

name: Helping behavior
definition: Going beyond the formal job description to engage in activities that benefit immediate colleagues, such as helping behavior, a form of organizational citizenship behavior.

name: Norm violator reputation
authors_terms: ["reputation of the violator", "reputation", "highly regarded chef", "reputable player"]
definition: The standing of the norm violator in the eyes of the community. The authors state that a chef's reputation acts as a kind of signaling device, allowing community members to assess the individual's propensity to violate a norm, and that sanctioning highly reputed players bears a higher social cost because the community will afford them the benefit of the doubt.

name: Public scrutiny
authors_terms: ["public scrutiny", "public attention", "level of public attention", "frequency of review"]
definition: Public scrutiny of the presumed norm violator, that is, the level of public attention the violator attracts.

name: Competition with the norm violator
authors_terms: ["degree of competition", "closer degree of competition", "physical proximity", "similarity of positioning", "local competitors"]
definition: The degree of competition between two industry players, which the authors report to be a function of the overlap of customers and which in turn depends on both physical proximity and similarity in positioning. Competition indicates an ongoing relationship that is subject to tit-for-tat discipline and suggests a homogenous understanding of norms and sanctions.

name: Norm violation severity
authors_terms: ["severity of a norm", "severity of the violation", "severity of a norm violation", "type of knowledge"]
definition: The severity of the norm violation, which depends on the nature of the object of the violation and in particular on its distinctiveness to the offended party. The authors state that the type of knowledge being misused drives this feeling of distinctiveness, violations entailing recipes of signature dishes being the most severe.

name: Propensity to sanction
authors_terms: ["propensity to sanction", "propensity to sanction a norm violation", "administration of sanctions", "propensity to administer a sanction"]
definition: An individual's propensity to sanction a norm violation described in the scenario. The authors report three types of sanctions commonly used for violations of norms proscribing the use of transferred culinary knowledge: refusing future knowledge transfers, cutting off material exchanges, and sharing negative gossip with colleagues.

name: Propensity to transfer knowledge
authors_terms: ["propensity to transfer knowledge", "propensity to cooperate", "propensity to participate", "participation in social exchange"]
definition: The likelihood that a respondent would transfer culinary knowledge to the chef described in the scenario; the authors describe knowledge transfer as a particular case of participation in the norm-governed exchange.

name: Ritual enactment participation
authors_terms: ["ritual enactment", "participating in the ritualistic conferment of prestige", "Participation in the ASG", "participation in the ASG"]
definition: Ritual enactment is triggered when tournament winners participate in a ritualistic bestowal of prestige, such as the conferment of an award in tournament rituals; the authors treat participation in the NBA All-Star Game as representing an enactment of a ritualistic conferment of professional prestige.

name: Productivity
definition: The rate at which an individual transforms inputs into outputs; the authors operationalize players' productivity by calculating ratios of overall performance to the levels of input received.

name: Inputs received
definition: The resources or opportunities that input providers give to a focal actor, which the authors consider a relational process whose outcome is determined by 'who takes the initiative to take [resources] and use them, and who passively accepts that these material objects are also used.' The relevant input providers are those who can provide (or withhold) players with resources or opportunities that can directly influence their individual performance on court, namely coaches and teammates.

name: Overall performance
definition: A composite assessment of a player's overall performance for each game that incorporates information on, for instance, failed attempts to score, turning over the ball, or possessions by the opposing team that a player stopped, blocked, or retrieved.

name: Time elapsed since ritual enactment
definition: Time measured in games since the ritual: the boost in emotional energy that ritual enactment generates in participants is transitory by nature, so the more time that passes after ritual enactment, the more likely it is that emotional energy levels will return to a baseline state.

name: Geographic proximity
definition: Geographic colocation indicates whether the star and nonstar scientists were based in the same geographic area, within the same commuting area so that they had the opportunity to regularly participate in face-to-face seminars, workshops, and other social foci.

name: Network proximity
definition: A third-party tie exists between a nonstar and a star scientist when both have a collaboration tie with a third scientist.

name: First-time collaboration tie formation
definition: First-time collaboration is a dyadic dichotomous variable set to 1 if the star and nonstar scientist collaborated for the first time in the current year, as observed by coauthoring a patent application.

name: Nonstar scientist gender
definition: Female nonstar is a dummy variable for the gender of the nonstar scientists.

name: Star scientist gender
authors_terms: ["star scientist's gender", "gender of the star", "Female star", "Male star"]
definition: The gender of the star scientist, used in a set of dummy variables combining the gender of the star and nonstar scientist.

name: Individual experience
definition: Individual experience-the cumulative production history of any one individual-provides an individual with an opportunity to become more proficient at his or her tasks and at performing established routines and practices.

name: Organizational experience
definition: Organizational experience-the cumulative production history of the organization-provides the organization with the opportunity to identify more productive routines and practices. As the organization gains more experience, each individual has more opportunities to benefit from knowledge accumulated by others.

name: Team experience
definition: Experience working together-the cumulative production history of pairs of individuals-provides individuals with the opportunity to learn who knows what, resulting in a more efficient division of labor. We call this variable team experience.

name: Procedure completion time
definition: Our performance metric is the amount of time it takes for a surgical team to complete a total joint replacement. We use reductions in procedure time as an indicator of organizational learning.

name: Interfunctional conflict
definition: The perceived differences in goals and ideologies across the three interdependent and interactive functions of marketing, R&D, and manufacturing.

name: New product success
authors_terms: ["new product success", "new product performance", "NPD success", "innovation success"]
definition: Respondents' perceptions of new product success in four dimensions: the company's relative success level in the industry, its NPD success relative to its objective, its NPD success relative to competitors in cycle time, quality, product line width and market share, and the timing of new product introductions.

name: Avoidance conflict resolution
definition: A conflict resolution approach that combines low assertiveness with low concern for others; when avoidance is used to resolve conflicts, conflicts are ignored rather than confronted.

name: Accommodation conflict resolution
definition: An approach to conflict resolution in which one party yields to the wishes of the other; rather than combining two diverse viewpoints, a one-sided decision is made.

name: Competitive conflict resolution
definition: A conflict resolution approach that combines high assertiveness with low concern for others; power is used to get one's own way regardless of the wishes of the other party.

name: Collaborative conflict resolution
definition: An approach to conflict resolution that combines high assertiveness with high concern for others; participants work cooperatively toward a win-win solution by bringing all relevant issues into the open, sharing information, and analyzing the situation objectively.

name: Compromise conflict resolution
definition: An approach intermediate in concern for self and others; the two parties take into account their respective wishes and settle at some intermediate point between their preferred positions.

name: Hierarchical conflict resolution
authors_terms: ["hierarchical resolution", "hierarchical method", "referral up the chain of command"]
definition: An approach to organizational conflict resolution that entails appealing to a joint superior when the conflicting NPD functions are unable to resolve their disagreements.

name: National culture
definition: People in different cultures have different ideologies that determine the basic assumptions shared by people in a particular society; the authors characterize cultures with Hofstede's dimensions of individualism, power distance, uncertainty avoidance, masculinity and long-term orientation.

name: Environmental volatility
definition: Environmental volatility refers to the level of instability or unpredictability faced by an organizational unit; the authors view it as the unpredictability in access to and utilization of key resources required by an organizational unit.

name: Standard component design
authors_terms: ["standard component designs", "standard design", "standard components", "use of standard components", "modular design with standard components"]
definition: A standard software component refers to a particular design for a software module or program that is widely used across software products within a firm or in software products used by many firms; it can be developed internally or purchased.

name: Process technology
authors_terms: ["process technology", "CASE tools", "CASE tool automation", "CASE tool use", "computer-aided software engineering tools"]
definition: The use of process technology, i.e., CASE tool automation; computer-aided software engineering (CASE) tools automate the analysis and development process by providing facilities for diagramming, requirements specification, design, quality management, documentation, and generation of models and code.

name: Team rotation
authors_terms: ["team rotation", "rotation of a software product's team members", "rotating developers", "new developer-component assignments"]
definition: Rotating members across tasks and projects, so that new developers are assigned to work on a software product and updates are made by a team member other than the one who completed the previous change.

name: Enhancement volatility
definition: Enhancement volatility refers to the length of time between software product enhancements and to the magnitude of the enhancements, where enhancements are activities that modify or extend the functionality of the software product, including the addition of new features.

name: Corrective volatility
definition: Corrective volatility refers to the length of time between software product repairs and to the magnitude of the repairs, where corrections are activities to repair software product defects.

name: Division-of-labor organization
authors_terms: ["division-of-labor form of organization", "division-of-labor organization", "division-of-labor groups", "organization structure", "functional decentralization", "decentralized organization"]
definition: The division-of-labor group enjoyed the advantages of participation and, in addition, had a decision structure-each man being responsible for one of the three decisions.

name: Problem-solving efficiency
authors_terms: ["problem-solving efficiency", "quality of solution", "achieved levels of profit", "relative profit", "percentage of potential profit"]
definition: Quality of solution in the complex business game, indexed by achieved levels of profit; problem-solving efficiency was measured as the percentage of potential profit achieved for each trial.

name: Learning rate
authors_terms: ["time (number of trials) required to solve the game", "rate of improvement in performance", "rates of learning", "rates of adaptation", "rates of progress to criterion"]
definition: The rate of improvement in performance over trials, indexed by the b parameter of the power function learning curve; for a given level of initial performance, larger b values indicate faster rates of improvement in performance.

name: Task variety
authors_terms: ["task variety", "variety", "stimulus uncertainty", "uncertainty about the occurrence of problems and exceptions"]
definition: Task variety is the frequency of unexpected and novel events that occur in the conversion process. Variety represents what might be called stimulus uncertainty for participants.

name: Task analyzability
definition: Task analyzability concerns how individuals respond to problems that arise: when the conversion process is analyzable, participants typically follow an objective, computational procedure to resolve problems. When work processes are not analyzable, participants experience response uncertainty.

name: Amount of information processing
authors_terms: ["amount of information processing", "information amount", "amount of task information processed", "information-processing activity"]
definition: The amount of information processing is defined as the volume or quantity of data about organizational activities that is gathered and interpreted by organization participants.

name: Information equivocality
definition: Information equivocality is defined as the multiplicity of meaning conveyed by information about organizational activities. Information that lends itself to different and perhaps conflicting interpretations about the work context is equivocal.

name: Group longevity
authors_terms: ["group longevity", "mean project tenure", "mean group tenure", "mean tenure of project group members", "stability in project membership"]
definition: Group longevity is not the length of time the project has been in existence, but the average length of time project members have interacted with each other.

name: Communication outside the project group
authors_terms: ["communication with relevant information sources outside their project groups", "contacts outside the project group", "outside contact"]
definition: Work-related oral communication of project members with relevant information sources outside the project group, both within and outside the organization.

name: Intraproject communication
authors_terms: ["intraproject communication", "intragroup interaction", "interaction among all project members", "interactions among themselves"]
definition: Communication reported among all members of the project group.

name: Internal communication
definition: Technical communication by project members with information sources within the organization; measured by intraproject, departmental, laboratory and organizational communication.

name: External communication
authors_terms: ["external communication", "external communications", "external professional communication", "contacts between project members and professional colleagues outside the organization"]
definition: Contacts between project members and professional colleagues outside the organization; measured by professional and operational communication.

name: Project performance
definition: The overall technical performance of a project as judged by the department managers and laboratory directors technically familiar with it, considering criteria such as schedule, budget and cost performance, innovativeness, adaptability, and the ability to cooperate with other groups in the organization.

name: Project task type
authors_terms: ["type of work", "nature of the project's work", "project categories", "research, development, and technical service project groups"]
definition: The nature of a project's work, from basic research through applied research and development to technical service, differing in specific versus general problem-solving orientation and in generation of new knowledge versus utilization of existing knowledge.

name: National science policy influence
authors_terms: ["influence of national science policy on research-unit themes", "national science policy influence", "science policy influence", "policy influence", "influence from national science policy"]
definition: Influence from national science policymaking bodies, in the form of formal guidelines and instructions, on scientists' choice of research themes; a source of bureaucratic control in scientific settings.

name: Research productivity
definition: Research output in the form of books and articles published, used as a measure of the performance of research units.

name: Paradigm development
authors_terms: ["paradigm development", "level of paradigm development", "highly developed paradigms", "less developed paradigms"]
definition: The extent to which a scientific field's paradigm, the constellation of beliefs, values and techniques shared by its members, is developed; fields with more developed paradigms show more consensus on methodology and research questions and less uncertainty.

name: Formal authority structure
definition: The listing of reporting relations in the organization; the simplest of the task networks, which virtually every organization can provide.

name: Task structure
authors_terms: ["task or work flow structure", "task structure", "task relations", "task network", "work flow structure"]
definition: How the tasks relate to each other: with whom one must relate to accomplish his job; the task network indicates who must relate to whom as part of his job.

name: Physical proximity
definition: Spatial relations between persons, one of the categories of communications environment factors; distance can be measured from floor layout drawings and maps.

name: Written communication
authors_terms: ["written communication", "pattern of written communication", "written traffic", "written mode", "paper matter received"]
definition: Communication via the written mode, such as letters, memos, requisitions and reports received; the author notes its storage and multiple copy capability.

name: Telephone communication
authors_terms: ["telephone communication", "pattern of telephone communication", "telephone traffic", "telephone calls"]
definition: Communication via telephone calls, noted for its real-time feedback capability.

name: Face-to-face communication
definition: Personal visits received, any face-to-face conversation in one's work space, and face-to-face conferences.

name: Formal hierarchical rank
authors_terms: ["formal status", "formal hierarchical position", "formal administrative rank", "formal rank", "formal position in the hierarchy"]
definition: Formal position in the hierarchy is associated with assigned authority, responsibility, and discretion over a range of resources and decision areas.

name: Influence in decision making
authors_terms: ["influence in decision making", "influence in administrative and technical decision making", "perceived influence", "influence nominations", "nominated as influential"]
definition: Not defined explicitly; assessed by peer nominations of the most influential people in the laboratory whom the respondent personally tried to influence, asked for technical, budgetary and personnel decisions.

name: Boundary spanning role
definition: Boundary spanning individuals are strongly linked both within the unit (they are internal communication stars) and to external sources of information.

name: Internal communication star role
definition: Internal communication stars are those individuals most frequently approached as discussion partners, but who are not strongly linked to external sources of information.

name: External communication star role
definition: External communication stars are those individuals who are only linked to external sources and who are not well integrated into their unit's communication network.

name: Task uncertainty
authors_terms: ["task requirements", "work related uncertainty", "task uncertainty", "project task characteristics", "task dimension ranging from research to technical service", "task area"]
definition: In R&D settings, the locus of critical uncertainty and information differs across task areas: research and development projects face substantial technical and market based uncertainty, while technical service units have less task uncertainty and a greater reliance on local procedures, routines and precedent. Tasks differ by the length of time required for feedback, specific vs. general problem orientation, and generation of new knowledge vs. use of existing knowledge.

name: Business return
authors_terms: ["return", "business return", "average firm return over time", "average annual return", "accounting return", "RETURN"]
definition: A firm's average annual return over the study period: average annual after-tax net income, including extraordinary items, divided by the book value of its stockholders' equity.

name: Business risk
authors_terms: ["risk", "business risk", "financial risk", "variability of periodic returns", "variability of annual returns", "return variability", "RISK"]
definition: The variability of a firm's periodic (annual) returns over time, measured as deviations of annual returns around a trend line from an autoregressive time series model.

name: Financial leverage
authors_terms: ["debt", "debt ratio", "use of debt financing", "debt levels", "leverage", "DEBT", "debt financing"]
definition: The proportion of a firm's assets that are supported by borrowed funds.

name: Industry structure
definition: Industry factors considered were the rate and stability of industry growth, barriers to entry of new competitors, industry concentration, and the total number of competitors in the industry.

name: Business strategy
definition: Business strategy refers to broad multifunctional decisions and actions; the study examined sales growth, size, capital intensity, productivity, and the use of debt financing.

name: Industry growth
authors_terms: ["industry growth", "rate of growth in the sales of an industry", "industry sales growth"]
definition: The rate of growth in the sales of an industry.

name: Industry growth variability
authors_terms: ["stability of industry growth", "year-to-year variation in the rate of industry growth", "variability of sales growth"]
definition: Year-to-year variation in the rate of industry growth.

name: Entry barriers
authors_terms: ["barriers to entry", "barriers to the entry of new competitors", "entry barriers"]
definition: Barriers such as economies of scale, absolute capital requirements, switching costs, and government policy that keep potential competitors from entering an industry.

name: Industry concentration
definition: Seller concentration of an industry, captured as four-firm sales concentration.

name: Number of competitors
authors_terms: ["number of firms in an industry", "number of industry competitors", "total number of competitors"]
definition: The total number of competitors (firms) in the industry.

name: Business growth
definition: The firm's rate of sales growth, which may differ from the industry average across strategic groups.

name: Business growth variability
authors_terms: ["variability in the rate of business growth", "variability of sales growth"]
definition: Variability in the rate of business sales growth.

name: Firm size
definition: The size of the business, specified as the natural logarithm of business size.

name: Capital intensity
definition: The degree to which a firm is capital intensive; not defined further in the prose.

name: Productivity
definition: Firm productivity, which differs across firms because of individual skills, organizational capabilities and technological competence.

name: Level of evidence
authors_terms: ["level of evidence", "level of supporting evidence", "evidence", "level of published evidence"]
definition: The level of published evidence that suggests the portfolio of recommended practices will result in improved patient outcomes.

name: Learn-what
definition: A bundle of learning activities that identify best practices; these activities center on discovering existing best-practice information from the external environment.

name: Learn-how
definition: A bundle of learning activities to discover the underlying science of a new practice so as to operationalize the practice in a target organization.

name: Psychological safety
definition: The collective belief within a work unit that members can question existing practices and admit mistakes without suffering ridicule or punishment.

name: Implementation success
definition: Employee commitment to and consistent use of new practices.

name: Degree of standardization
authors_terms: ["degree of standardization", "standardization", "drug standardization", "formulary standardization", "restrictive formulary", "drug availability"]
definition: Standardization is the formulation and imposition of specific rules or choices created by authority; in this setting, high drug standardization is equivalent to low drug availability on the hospital formulary.

name: Cost effectiveness
authors_terms: ["cost effectiveness", "cost effectiveness of the hospital pharmacy", "hospital cost effectiveness", "daily pharmacy charge"]
definition: The cost effectiveness of the hospital pharmacy, measured by dividing the total pharmacy charge by the length of stay for each patient hospitalized.

name: Formal objectivity
definition: Whether decisions about standardized procedures are made according to objective standards or according to subjective preferences of individual decision makers.

name: Responsiveness
authors_terms: ["responsiveness", "responsive to the users of the standardized procedure"]
definition: Whether decision makers hear from those affected by the standardization decision.

name: Due process
definition: Whether appeal procedures exist for correcting bad decisions regarding standardization.

name: Allowing exceptions
definition: Whether decisions regarding standardization are implemented flexibly, allowing local discretion.

name: Dispersion in explained pay
definition: The amount of variation in the employee pay that is tied to productivity-relevant employee inputs.

name: Dispersion in unexplained pay
definition: The amount of variation in the employee pay that is unexplained by productivity-relevant inputs, attributable to factors unrelated to employee productivity.

name: Pay dispersion
definition: Lateral pay dispersion involves pay differences among employees within the same job or organizational level.

name: Productivity-relevant employee inputs
definition: Employee inputs (typically job performance) associated with organizational productivity.

name: Relationally loaded interorganizational ties
definition: Enduring ties characterized by their embedded nature and emotional intensity, typically symmetrical, based on friendship or antagonism.

name: Mobility along relationally loaded ties
authors_terms: ["career mobility along the same lines", "experience with allies/rivals", "temporal multiplexity"]
definition: A jockey's previous affiliations with allies and rivals of his current employer; temporal multiplexity is the overlaying of relationships of different duration.

name: Involvement in conflict
definition: An incident is an instance of conflict where one contrada, its jockey or members, engages in an altercation with one or more other contrade, jockey, or members before, during, or after the race.

name: Industrial relations research program
authors_terms: ["existence of an IR research program", "IR research"]
definition: Industrial relations research is purposive, systematic investigation and analysis of relationships which arise out of the employment process.

name: Achieved memory
definition: The amount of knowledge, experience, and familiarity with the supply chain process.

name: Knowledge acquisition
definition: Knowledge acquisition is one of the four key learning elements identified by Huber (1991); knowledge acquisition activities enhance each supply chain node's knowledge flows.

name: Information distribution
definition: Distribution of information among supply chain nodes, through which each node becomes more educated about how to operate within the chain and about other nodes' needs and preferences.

name: Shared meaning
definition: The extent to which participants develop common understandings about data and events.

name: Cycle time
definition: The interval between a user's request for a product or service and its delivery.

name: Funds requested
definition: The amount of funds requested from Congress by the FTC.

name: Funds appropriated
definition: The amount of funds appropriated for the FTC by Congress.

name: Applications for complaint
definition: Applications filed by aggrieved individuals and businesses, the initial workload input of the bureaus.

name: Investigations filed
definition: Number of investigations filed.

name: Investigations uncompleted
definition: Number of investigations that remain uncompleted.

name: Labor productivity
definition: Output of each of four workflow stages divided by the number of employees.

name: Capital productivity
definition: Output divided by funds received, constructed in two indexes.

name: Investigations completed
definition: Number of investigations completed by the bureaus, the initial high volume workflow output.

name: Staff size
definition: Number of employees of the FTC.

name: Average salary
definition: Average salary of FTC employees.

name: Formal complaints
definition: Bureaus' output of proposed formal complaints and orders.

name: Policy shift
definition: The FTC decision about 1964 to be more selective in choosing cases, increasing the role of voluntary compliance.

name: Cease and desist orders
definition: Hearing examiners' output of orders after prehearing conferences and trial.

name: Cases handled by hearing examiners
definition: Throughput measure of cases handled by the hearing examiners.

name: Litigations
definition: Cases litigated in federal courts by the Office of General Counsel.

name: Cases handled by general counsel
definition: Workload throughput of the Office of General Counsel.

name: Contested orders
definition: Number of orders contested by business respondents, reported from 1959.

name: Aggressiveness
definition: Ratio of contested orders to total orders.

name: Wage dispersion
definition: The degree of equality or dispersion of salaries within a department.

name: Variation in human capital
definition: Heterogeneity within a department in productivity, experience, rank, gender and range of duties.

name: Department size
definition: Size of the department estimated from faculty members' reports of regular members.

name: Working alone
authors_terms: ["proportion of the department that works alone", "tendency to work alone"]
definition: The percentage of department members who report working essentially alone on their current major research.

name: Social contact
definition: Social contact among faculty members, assessed from how many of the people they see socially are department members.

name: Private control
definition: Colleges and universities coded by the Carnegie Commission as privately controlled.

name: Chair appointment term length
authors_terms: ["length of the chairperson's term", "long, indefinite term"]
definition: Whether the department chair is appointed for a long or indefinite term rather than a fixed short term.

name: Participative decision making
definition: The proportion of department members who report that non-personnel decisions are made by vote of the whole department.

name: Autocratic governance
definition: Mean department rating of how autocratic the administration of the department is.

name: Representation of women
authors_terms: ["representation of high-skill women", "employment of women", "proportion of women in the firm"]
definition: The proportion of women in the firm's work force and in occupational categories, with a focus on high-skill positions such as managers and professionals.

name: Firm performance
definition: Firm performance indicated by return on assets, return on equity and growth in sales.

name: Firm nationality
definition: The nationality of the firm's home-country headquarters (U.S., Japan or Thailand).

name: Work attitudes
authors_terms: ["work attitudes", "organizational commitment, job satisfaction and relationship with supervisors"]
definition: Employees' organizational commitment, job satisfaction and the quality of their relationships with immediate supervisors.

name: Workplace gender segregation
definition: Establishment-level gender segregation among non-managerial workers, interpreted as the percentage of women or men that would have to change occupations to equalize the gender distributions across the occupations.

name: Women's representation in management
authors_terms: ["women's access to organizational power structures", "female managers", "women in management"]
definition: The percentage of female officials and managers in each establishment, used to capture women's representation in leadership positions.

name: Establishment size
definition: The total number of workers in the establishment.

name: Establishment growth
definition: The mean annualized growth rate of the establishment's total employment over the previous four-year period.

name: Time period
definition: The calendar year of observation, used to test whether the effect of female managers changes over time.

name: Plant size
definition: Plant size is a construct representing fixed investment, that is plant capacity rather than plant output.

name: Plant productivity
definition: Output per worker, estimated in a total factor productivity model controlling for factor inputs.

name: Time period
definition: The comparison of estimated parameters between 1972 and 1982.

name: Product focus
definition: The degree to which a plant concentrates on a narrow product mix, so that managerial complexity from product variety is lower.

name: Vertical integration
authors_terms: ["vertical integration at the plant level", "plant level vertical integration", "process focus"]
definition: Plant-level vertical integration, which combines upstream and downstream processes within the same plant; in a more vertically integrated plant management is involved in more tasks that may have different or conflicting demands. The authors use it to operationalize process focus, with lower integration meaning higher focus.

name: Supervisory overhead
authors_terms: ["supervisory overhead", "ratio of supervisory to direct workers"]
definition: Supervisory and indirect workers in a plant relative to direct production workers, which the authors see as layers used to manage complexity within the plant.

name: Industry technological change
authors_terms: ["technological level of the industry", "rate of technological change", "technological level of industries"]
definition: The technological level of the industry, ranked using research and development spending as a proxy for the rate of technological change.

name: Executive education level
definition: The level of formal education of top executives, from no college to doctorate.

name: Technical education of executives
authors_terms: ["technical level of the education of top executives"]
definition: The technical level of the education of top executives, examined for the undergraduate degree, Master's degree and Doctorate.

name: Executive job mobility
definition: The job mobility of top executives, which was not measured directly; length of service was used as a proxy.

name: Executive age
definition: The age of top executives, drawn from their date of birth.

name: Cohort concentration
authors_terms: ["dominant cohort", "proportion of the faculty entered the unit at the same time", "clustering of the department", "lumpiness of the department's distribution"]
definition: The extent to which there exists a dominant cohort, identified by having a large proportion of the present organizational membership having entered in a relatively short span of time.

name: Gaps between cohorts
authors_terms: ["large gaps between cohorts", "cleavages among cohorts", "gaps between cohorts"]
definition: Periods in which no new individuals were hired, producing well-differentiated cohorts with different norms and expectations.

name: Turnover
definition: The amount of turnover experienced by the department, including voluntary resignations, early retirements and involuntary expired appointments, excluding deaths and mandatory retirements.

name: Resource practices
definition: Identity-conscious, opportunity-based and preferential treatment practices that provide targets with additional support and opportunities.

name: Non-discrimination practices
definition: Practices that focus on merit-based decisions, ignoring or equally weighing demographics for hiring, promotions and assignments, aimed at decreasing bias and discrimination.

name: Accountability practices
definition: Practices aimed at increasing responsibility for, and monitoring of, diversity goals.

name: Employee turnover
authors_terms: ["turnover rate among women and racialized non-leaders", "turnover rate among women and racialized leaders", "turnover rate", "turnover"]
definition: Turnover of women and racialized employees, measured as the share of non-leaders (associates) or leaders (partners) who departed the firm during a year.

name: Turnover intention
definition: Participants' intention to leave the fictional company.

name: Concerns about unfair treatment
definition: Attitudinal perceptions of worry that being a beneficiary of resource practices may result in unfair and biased treatment in the organization.

name: Personal relevance
definition: Assessments of a practice's usefulness and importance, as judgments about whether practices are applicable to oneself and the achievement of one's goals.

name: Government size
definition: Size of government is indicated most directly by the number of full-time government employees within a county.

name: Number of administrative units
authors_terms: ["number of administrative units", "multiplicity of administrative units", "ADM"]
definition: The number of local government units with property tax power within a county, such as the county government, municipalities, school districts and a few special districts.

name: Perceived quality of public services
authors_terms: ["quality of services", "citizens' perceptions of the quality of common public services"]
definition: Citizens' evaluation of the quality of a package of common public services in their county.

name: Goal specificity
authors_terms: ["goal specificity", "specificity of the organizational goal structure"]
definition: The presence of well-defined and empirically observable organizational outputs and testable linkings between certain organizational activities and the accomplishment of these outputs.

name: Use of output measures in evaluation
definition: Evaluation based on ascertaining the contributions of those being evaluated to organizational goals or outputs.

name: Use of performance measures in evaluation
definition: Evaluation based on how a task is performed rather than on the impact of the task on output.

name: Use of efficiency measures in evaluation
definition: Evaluation criteria such as savings in unit costs of outputs or services, in manpower costs and in equipment costs.

name: Interdependence
definition: The extent to which the organization's task requires its members to work with one another.

name: Coordination
definition: The extent to which the work activities of organizational members are logically consistent and coherent.

name: Unit output
definition: Unit performance assessed in terms of the quality and quantity of the unit's research output.

name: Employee voice mechanisms
definition: Mechanisms, whether union mandated or not, that organizations put in place to enhance employees' opportunities for voicing dissatisfaction.

name: Voluntary turnover
authors_terms: ["voluntary turnover rate", "employee retention", "turnover among registered nurses"]
definition: Rate of voluntary turnover among the organization's registered nurses.

name: Expectancy of problem resolution
authors_terms: ["expectancies for resolving work related problems", "expectancy of problem resolution"]
definition: Nurses' estimates of how often they would be effective in resolving work-related problems.

name: Perceived effectiveness of voice mechanisms
authors_terms: ["effectiveness of problem resolution procedures", "perceived effectiveness of voice mechanisms"]
definition: Employees' perceptions of the general effectiveness of their organizations' voice mechanisms.

name: Pay level
authors_terms: ["pay level", "minimum pay", "midpoint of the pay range"]
definition: The level of pay a firm offers, measured by the minimum and the midpoint of the stated pay range for tellers.

name: Benefits
definition: Benefit programs measured by variables designed to capture both the level of benefits provided and their flexibility, the degree to which they are tailored to employees' needs.

name: Number of applicants
authors_terms: ["number of teller applicants", "size of an applicant pool"]
definition: The number of applicants a firm attracts to a job.

name: Acceptance rate
definition: The rate at which applicants accept the job offers an employer makes.

name: Time to fill positions
authors_terms: ["length of time it takes to fill positions", "time position open"]
definition: The length of time it takes a firm to fill its positions.

name: Idiosyncratic job creation
definition: Jobs whose existence was prompted by the jobholder and whose combination of activities was designed to match that person's perceived abilities, interests or priorities; evolved jobs develop around current employees and opportunistic hires around newcomers.

name: Formalization
definition: The extent to which rules governing behavior are precisely and explicitly formulated and roles are prescribed independently of the individuals occupying positions.

name: Resource uncertainty
definition: Indeterminacy about what will happen with resources; the questionnaire item asks about the degree of uncertainty in total resources.

name: Mission ambiguity
definition: Indeterminacy in the meaning of what happens, including diffuse or conflicting organizational preferences or poorly understood methods for known goals.

name: Resource variation
definition: Variety in the resources and opportunities available to the organization; the item asks how varied and unpredictable the sources of support are.

name: Problem variation
definition: A high level of variation of current and potential problems the unit faces.

name: Financial flexibility
definition: Access to resources that might fund unanticipated projects, allow a change in course mid-stream or permit an unanticipated increase in funds spent on existing projects.

name: Change in organizational size
authors_terms: ["change in size", "change in organizational size (number of employees)"]
definition: Growth or decline in the number of employees of a unit over the study period.

name: Senior management uncertainty about the IS function
authors_terms: ["principal's level of uncertainty about the IS function", "superior's uncertainty"]
definition: The level of uncertainty faced by an organization's senior managers with respect to the activities the IS function must undertake.

name: IS manager uncertainty about the IS function
authors_terms: ["agent's level of uncertainty about the IS function", "IS manager uncertainty"]
definition: The level of uncertainty faced by the IS manager relating to the activities the IS function must undertake.

name: Dependency of senior management on the IS manager
authors_terms: ["relative dependency", "dependency of the principal on the agent", "relative level of specificity of senior management's assets versus the IS manager's assets", "relative balance of cospecialization"]
definition: The relative balance of cospecialization between senior management and the IS manager, that is, how specific each party's assets are to the relationship.

name: Delegation of decision rights
authors_terms: ["delegation of decision rights to the IS manager"]
definition: The level of decision rights delegated to the IS manager.

name: Amount of IS planning
authors_terms: ["IS planning", "planning that is more detailed, more time consuming, and more complex"]
definition: Higher levels of IS planning mean planning that is more detailed, more time consuming, and more complex.

name: Senior management control of IS planning process
authors_terms: ["control over the IS planning process", "principal controlled or agent controlled planning process", "superior controlled versus IS manager controlled planning process"]
definition: The degree to which senior management rather than the IS manager exerts most influence on planning activities; the authors characterize the process as principal controlled or agent controlled.

name: Focus of IS plan on senior management goals
authors_terms: ["focus of the final IS plan", "principal focused or agent focused IS plan", "superior focused versus IS manager focused plan"]
definition: Whether the final IS plan primarily reflects senior management's goals (principal focused) or the IS manager's goals (agent focused).

name: Usefulness of IS plan for monitoring, bonding and governance
authors_terms: ["usefulness of the IS plan for monitoring, bonding, and governance purposes"]
definition: Senior management's view of the plan's usefulness as a monitoring, bonding and governance device, for example as a basis for compensating the IS manager.

name: Ex post agency costs
definition: The estimated level of agency costs that exists after the employment contract has been exchanged, an equilibrium level reached after negotiation between principal and agent.

name: Organizational failure
definition: Firms in the sample filed Chapter X or XI bankruptcy petitions and are compared with matched survivors; failure is described as a protracted downward spiral.

name: Top management team composition
definition: TMTs of failing firms may differ, or diverge, systematically in their composition from top teams of successful, healthy organizations; divergence is expected to increase over time (deterioration). Two classes of attributes are studied: team resources (team size, outside directors, functional expertise, team compensation) and team social structure (average tenure, tenure heterogeneity, CEO dominance).

name: Organizational performance
definition: Profitability of the firm, measured as return on assets, relative to matched survivors.

name: Proximity to bankruptcy
authors_terms: ["as the failures approach bankruptcy", "last five years of the bankrupts' lives"]
definition: Years before the year of bankruptcy t, from t-5 to t-1; higher proximity means closer to bankruptcy.

name: Top team size
definition: The resources available on a team result from how many people are on it.

name: Outside directors
definition: Board members who were not officers of the firm, who supplement the team's knowledge base.

name: Core functional expertise
definition: The mix of functional expertise on a team, in particular representation of core functional areas of design, production and marketing.

name: Team compensation
definition: Pay of the team, an indirect way of assessing the quality of a team.

name: Average team tenure
definition: The TMT's average tenure in the firm, which may indicate cohesion.

name: Tenure heterogeneity
definition: The dispersion of tenures within the team, reflecting whether members belong to the same or different cohorts in the firm.

name: CEO dominance
definition: Presence of a dominant CEO or autocrat on the top team.

name: Vertical integration
definition: The percentage of the system produced in house, with 1 indicating in-house production of all components within that system.

name: Initial performance
definition: Short-Term Performance is a measure of the performance measure during the first two years of the product life cycle (inclusive of the introduction year).

name: Performance improvement
definition: The level of change in performance over the product life cycle, constructed as Long-Term Performance minus Short-Term Performance.

name: Ex ante experience
authors_terms: ["ex ante experience or knowledge", "ex ante capabilities", "ex ante internal capabilities"]
definition: The level of ex ante internal capabilities, identified in the empirical work by Japan OEM and Sunk Cost.

name: Access to globally innovative suppliers
authors_terms: ["globally innovative external contractor", "Innovative Supplier System", "Innovative Supplier Availability"]
definition: System-specific measure of the opportunity to access globally innovative suppliers, based on the availability of globally available innovative suppliers during the sample period.

name: Learning opportunities
definition: The opportunities for learning over the product life cycle, which vary across components and systems; identified in the empirical work by Platform.

name: Self-regulation adoption
authors_terms: ["self-regulation for reputation-sensitive buyers", "SA8000 certification", "adopting self-regulatory institutions"]
definition: Voluntary institutions through which firms commit to observe standards of corporate conduct beyond what is legally required, often formalized through certification to a self-regulatory standard.

name: Social performance
definition: The social and environmental practices of the firm, studied here through the wages paid to workers.

name: Exports
definition: Sales to buyers abroad; sales to reputation-sensitive buyers in advanced economies would appear as exports for supplier firms located elsewhere.

name: Domestic sales
definition: Total value of industrial products produced or services provided by the enterprise for domestic sales.

name: Employment
definition: Count of employees in the enterprise.
